north_star: Five-second fleet verification; earned calm — nothing fabricated, failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority; every clause a door on an unbroken trace spine (signal → session → evidence); keyboard-first; one visual language (Dispatch) built by one hand; plus the th-engineering bar and the th-projects mandates.

audits.page: /butlers (ButlersPage status board: BoardHeader, NeedsYouStrip, StatusBoardCell grid, BoardFooter; hook use-butler-status-board.ts over GET /api/butlers/board)
audits.jarvis_gap: The board is structurally strong — single round-trip payload, server-side canonical liveness verdict shared with Overview, needs-you strip with reason lines, degraded-source honesty on spend/sessions, restore-with-undo — but it falls short of the JARVIS bar in three ways. First, the page has no truthful freshness contract: the header caption asserts 'refreshes every 30s' while the real mechanism is bus-aware (live invalidation + 5-minute reconcile sweep when the bus is open), no dataUpdatedAt is surfaced anywhere, and the stale-data banner admits staleness without saying how stale — the flagship five-second-verification surface cannot prove its own currency. Second, the trace spine breaks at the cadence clause: a 5-minute-cadence butler flagged OVERDUE carries the evidence line 'silent 12m, expected hourly', which contradicts the verdict it is supposed to justify — a clause whose door opens onto evidence that disproves it. Third, the hot loop is mouse-only within the page (siblings SessionsPage/ButlerDetailPage/ChroniclesPage all register page shortcuts; the board registers none), needs-you clauses land on the butler-detail lobby rather than the evidence for the stated reason, and the page's vocabulary drifts ('All 12 butlers healthy' counting 3 staffers; 'Active' meaning running-now in the footer but eligibility in the rail). None of these fabricate health, but together they mean the owner must trust rather than verify the board's currency, and must re-hunt after every needs-you click.
audits.ideal: The owner lands on /butlers and in under five seconds knows whether the staff needs them and can prove it: a needs-you strip whose every clause is a door straight to the evidence for that clause (a quarantine reason opens the quarantining incident/session, an overdue clause opens the schedule that defines the expectation), a header that states its true freshness contract ('live via event bus, reconciled 12s ago' or 'bus down, polling 30s, data 25s old') with the stale banner carrying an exact age, cadence verdicts whose stated expectation is the butler's actual cron interval so the evidence always justifies the verdict, full keyboard operability (arrows/j-k across cells, Enter to open, r to restore-with-undo on a focused quarantined cell, listed in the ? sheet), one vocabulary shared by strip, pill, and footer, and restore feedback that is per-butler truthful under concurrency — all rendered in one Dispatch dialect.

findings.title: Board asserts a false freshness contract and surfaces no data age anywhere
findings.detail: BoardHeader prints 'refreshes every 30s' from hardcoded REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=30_000, but since bu-01r64.3 (fcf4b0c14) useButlersBoard polls via useBusAwarePollInterval: 5 minutes (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS) while the event bus is open, 30s only while it is down; primary updates ride bus session events, and eligibility/quarantine changes made elsewhere have NO bus event so they can take up to 5 minutes to appear while the caption promises 30s. No component on the page surfaces boardQuery.dataUpdatedAt, and the stale-data banner ('Showing last known butler status') gives the failure message but not the age of the cached rows. The five-second-verification page cannot prove its own currency — staleness wears current-data authority behind a fabricated cadence claim.

findings.title: Cadence evidence line contradicts the overdue verdict it justifies (5-min cadence labeled 'hourly')
findings.detail: _cadence_label buckets any cadence <= 7200s as 'hourly', while overdue fires at cadence_seconds * 2. Live: chronicler and most butlers have cadence_seconds=300.0 (5-min cron) with cadence_label='hourly'. A butler silent 12 minutes is verdict=OVERDUE, and NeedsYouStrip renders its reason as 'silent 12m, expected hourly' — an evidence line that reads as healthy for the verdict it is attached to. Same distortion in StatusBoardCell's cadenceTooltip ('Silent 12m, expected hourly'). The clause's door opens onto evidence that disproves the clause; the owner cannot audit why the butler is flagged.

findings.title: Concurrent restores lose per-butler pending truth (single-slot mutation variables)
findings.detail: isRestorePending for a cell is scheduledRestores.has(name) || networkPendingName === name, where networkPendingName = setEligibility.variables?.name of the LATEST mutate call. If the owner restores two butlers and their undo windows elapse close together, the first butler's chip drops RESTORING… while its network call is still in flight (variables now point at the second), becomes clickable again, and a re-click schedules a second restore for a butler whose first restore is mid-flight. Feedback is untruthful exactly during the overlap window.

audits.page: /calendar (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx, 7,180 lines + use-calendar-workspace.ts + calendar_workspace.py). NOTE: task brief said the dev stack was UP at 127.0.0.1:42200, but at audit time every butlers-dev container was in "Created" (not running) state and both 42200 and 42173 refused connections (curl: connection refused; docker ps confirms only log-cleanup running; no dev DB). All findings are therefore source-confirmed by reading the exact mechanisms — none live-confirmed. Shipped-since-baseline on this surface: #3336 Dispatch CTA conflict fixes, #3362 shared action-result recovery, #3366 keyed workspace reads, cfc369b55 workspace integration. The truth-spine work (freshness plaque, deadman, dedup radar, failed_butlers fan-out honesty, entries/people/audit source_available flags, undo-from-audit with distinct 404/409/422 messages, session links from audit rows and the detail panel) is genuinely strong and consumed, not decorative.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the surface's honesty spine is largely in place — freshness plaque, degraded notes that name their source, undo ghosts, session-linked audit — but it stands on a broken time foundation: the page is the only major workspace that bypasses the owner-timezone contract entirely, mixing three timezone authorities (browser Intl at line 2494, hardcoded "Asia/Singapore" in the backend meta, and the workspace grid renderer), so the masthead labels the grid with a timezone it does not render in, click-to-create books a different hour than the row clicked whenever the browser leaves SGT, and the recurrence preview's own caption contradicts its own rows. For a calendar — the one surface whose whole job is time — that is failure wearing current-data authority in the most literal sense, and it breaks exactly when the owner travels, which is when a JARVIS calendar matters most. Second, the proactive loop is muffled: butlers extract proposals and park them behind an unbadged "Proposals" pill whose query doesn't even run until the door is opened, so the system does work the owner cannot see without an act of faith — the opposite of five-second verification. Third, small truth leaks remain: an optimistic source-toggle that lies for up to 60s on the no-owning-butler path, and a pagination walker that forges has_more:false after its safety cap.

findings.title: Calendar workspace bypasses the owner-timezone contract — three competing timezone authorities on one page
findings.evidence: Spec openspec/specs/owner-timezone-context/spec.md ('Browser locale is never used as the default'; useTimezone()/AppTimezoneProvider mandatory, mounted at frontend/src/App.tsx:18). CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx contains zero useTimezone() calls (grep count 0) and instead reads Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone at frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2494 and :7005. Backend hardcodes the workspace tz as a literal: src/butlers/api/routers/calendar_workspace.py:1839 (default_timezone="Asia/Singapore") and :177 (_OVERLAY_DEFAULT_TZ), while sessions.py:448 already resolves owner tz from DB (_owner_zoneinfo_from_db) — the owner-tz spine exists and calendar ignores it.
findings.detail: Concrete user-facing breaks whenever browser tz != Asia/Singapore (i.e., whenever the owner travels): (a) masthead eyebrow at :4696 prints the BROWSER tz while every grid time renders in defaultTimezone (SGT) — a true grid under a false timezone caption (taxonomy shape 10); (b) click-to-create at :5664-5671 computes the slot via browser-local new Date(day).setHours(...) while drag-create at :3670-3695 correctly uses isoAtMinuteInTz(day, min, defaultTimezone) — clicking the 14:00 row prefills a dialog offset by the tz delta, drag on the same grid does not; (c) recurrence preview caption at :7005 claims browser tz while its occurrence rows at :7022-7024 format in defaultTimezone — self-contradicting component; (d) 'today' markers (isToday at :5510, month grid :5350) and the day-briefing 'Tomorrow' date param (:2740-2743, browser-local startOfDay) drift a day off the workspace date at the boundary; (e) butler-event dialog parses datetime-local inputs browser-local (parseLocalDateTimeInput → toISOString) while user-event forms parse in the form timezone — two parse conventions in one page.

findings.title: Pending butler proposals are invisible until the unbadged Proposals door is opened on faith
findings.evidence: Proposals query enabled only while the panel is open: CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2782-2785 ({ enabled: proposalsPanelOpen }) and use-calendar-workspace.ts:317-333. The toolbar 'Proposals' pill at :4857-4868 carries no count/badge; the pending count renders only inside the already-open panel (frontend/src/components/calendar/CalendarProposalsPanel.tsx:260 '{visible.length} pending'). Backend meta response (calendar_workspace.py:1835-1842) carries no proposal count. ConflictRadarBanner surfaces only conflict-fix proposals, and only on week/day ranges (:5442-5493).
findings.detail: Butler-extracted candidate events (the system's proactive work product awaiting an owner decision) generate zero ambient signal on the page that hosts them: no badge, no palette entry, no fetch while closed. An owner who never clicks the pill never learns proposals exist — a drill-down door with no light on it, the inverse of the five-second-verification bar and of the Decision Desk direction (bu-ckkpz covers attention citizens elsewhere; this calendar-local count badge is not in that epic's scope nor in bu-24lu6's Telegram scope).

findings.title: Source sync-toggle: optimistic flip is never reverted on the no-owning-butler early return — UI lies for up to 60s
findings.evidence: CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2597-2610 — setDisabledSources flips optimistically at :2601-2606, then `if (!source.butler_name) { toast.error(...); return; }` at :2607-2610 returns WITHOUT reverting; the mutation is never fired so toggleSourceMutation.isPending never changes, and the re-seed effect at :2579-2585 only re-runs when connectedSources identity changes (meta refetchInterval 60s, use-calendar-workspace.ts:212).
findings.detail: For a source whose owning butler cannot be resolved, the Sources dialog shows the sync toggle in its new state (enabled/disabled) for up to a full meta poll cycle even though nothing was persisted — success-state feedback for work that didn't happen (taxonomy shape 2, transient form). Fix is two lines (revert before return), or better: render the toggle disabled when butler_name is null, matching how the per-source Sync/Recover buttons already disable (:6307-6325).

findings.title: Keyset walker forges has_more:false after its 20-page safety cap — silent truncation wears complete-window authority
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-calendar-workspace.ts:76-97 — the loop breaks at WORKSPACE_MAX_PAGES (20 × 500 = 10,000 entries) and then unconditionally rewrites the envelope with `next_cursor: null, has_more: false` (:94-96); no flag reaches the page, so the grid and the masthead '{entries.length} events' count (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:4702-4704) present a truncated window as complete.
findings.detail: Unlikely in practice (needs >10k entries in one visible window) but it is a manufactured all-clear in exactly the code that exists to keep the window complete; the honest shape is a `truncated: true` passthrough rendered as a SourceDegradedNote like the sibling entries_source_available clause at :5140-5147.

findings.title: Overlap edge uses raw Tailwind amber-500 instead of the Dispatch --amber token
findings.evidence: CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:5809 ('border-l-2 border-l-amber-500') vs the sibling ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:110/:211/:216 which uses var(--amber)/var(--amber-text), and frontend/src/index.css:98/:139 which defines the canonical tokens (index.css is normative for values).
findings.detail: One-line dialect drift: the amber conflict edge on grid blocks is the same semantic signal as the radar banner but sourced from a different palette, so a Tailwind config change or theme adjustment would split the two ambers. Adjacent to (not covered by) bu-rqbcx, which sweeps raw-hex CHART colors.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade calendar workspace is the owner's single time authority: every timestamp on the page — grid placement, masthead caption, today markers, quick-add parsing, recurrence previews, briefing dates — resolves through one owner-timezone spine (useTimezone() → GET /api/settings/general → the same DB-resolved zone the backend uses for windows and overlays), with the browser zone appearing only as an explicit, labeled secondary ("14:00 SGT · 07:00 your local") when they diverge. It opens to a week that proves its own freshness (plaque + deadman, already landed), where conflicts, duplicates, and butler proposals each carry an ambient count the instant they exist — a "3 proposals" badge that can be triaged with j/k + accept/dismiss keys without opening a modal — so the owner verifies in five seconds that the butlers scheduled, deduped, and flagged correctly, and every event, proposal, and audit row remains one keystroke from its originating session evidence. Every optimistic control either commits or visibly reverts within the same interaction, and every completeness claim (event counts, window bounds, search results) is either true or wears a named degraded clause.

moves.why: Spec openspec/specs/owner-timezone-context/spec.md is explicit ('Browser locale is never used as the default') and the calendar is its largest violator; vision.md's bar is 'reliability, not novelty' and earned calm — a calendar whose caption, click-target, and preview label disagree about what timezone they're in fails 'staleness never wears current-data authority' in its most literal form, precisely when the owner travels. (2) BE: replace calendar_workspace.py:1839 hardcoded default_timezone and :177 _OVERLAY_DEFAULT_TZ with the general-settings owner tz (reuse sessions.py's _owner_zoneinfo_from_db, hoisted to a shared helper). findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py:708-812 (compose_briefing_payload — no read of daily_rollup_flags anywhere in editorial.py; grep 'flags' in the module returns nothing) vs roster/chronicler/api/router.py:2007-2016 (_dark_sources_from_flags) consumed at router.py:2090 (/balance lane unavailable=), and TrendsLens.tsx:8-10 ('per-day unavailable (feeder_dark) bars render hatched, never counted as zero'). editorial.py:151 templated voice on an episode-less day: 'The day produced no projected episodes.' + :162-164 'Nothing needs attention.'; headline_for()→'Quiet day.' Nothing needs attention.' while the Balance/Trends panels below the fold on the same page hatch those very lanes as unavailable. findings.detail: The state_class/headline derivation (classify_state at editorial.py:106-118) keys solely on attention_items, and attention items only cover sleep anomaly, interior waking gaps, live source health (recent days only), and open corrections. Coverage darkness never reaches the voice column, so failure impersonates health at the page's most authoritative position.

findings.title: Briefing backend swallows genuine DB failures into calm empties: source-health and earliest-date queries catch broad asyncpg.PostgresError and return []/None

Violates the fleet-wide convention in /home/tze/gt/butlers/CLAUDE.md §Degraded-Mode ('Classify before flagging… Getting this distinction wrong… reintroduces fabricated calm') and the reference classifier pattern (memory.py::_is_missing_memory_schema_error). The FE AttentionList primitive already has the isSourceError + onRetry affordance built for exactly this (frontend/src/components/overview/AttentionList.tsx:25-38) but the chronicles adapter never uses it (ChroniclesPage.tsx:115-123).

findings.title: KPI 'Longest gap' is threshold-censored, edge-blind, and shows 0 on a fully dark day
findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py:603-638 (_detect_waking_gaps: gaps computed only BETWEEN merged spans — 'for i in range(1, len(merged))'; window-start→first-episode and last-episode→window-end gaps never measured; empty spans → []), :631-637 (only gaps >= WAKING_GAP_ANOMALY_MINUTES=360 are returned at all), :687 (longest_gap = max(flagged) else 0). So a day whose longest waking gap is 5h59m renders 'Longest gap 0', a day tracked only 12:00-12:30 renders 'Longest gap 0', and a completely dark day renders 'Longest gap 0' — identical to a perfectly covered day. FE renders the number as a first-class KPI cell (ChroniclesPage.tsx:103-107, fmtMinutes(0) → '0'). The honest primitive already exists and is used by the gap interview + by-category untracked slice: aggregations.untracked_seconds_for_window (cited in roster/chronicler/AGENTS.md day-close gap interview notes and editorial.py:583-600 docstring).
findings.detail: Taxonomy shape 10 (mislabeled real data): the label promises 'longest gap'; the writer computes 'longest interior waking gap if >= 6h else 0'. The value's zero state is indistinguishable between full coverage and zero coverage.

findings.title: Silent 500-row truncation with DESC ordering drops the morning of dense days from the map trail, scrubber snap points, ribbon and Gantt — no indicator, meta.total ignored

A >500-point OwnTracks day (move mode easily exceeds this) yields a trail/scrubber/ribbon that silently covers only the evening tail while wearing full-day authority.
findings.detail: Partial data wearing complete-data authority, the exact staleness-authority sin, on the page whose whole premise is faithful reconstruction of a lived day.

findings.title: SourceStateBadgeStrip drops isError (strip vanishes on failure) and renders live-now adapter state undated on archive days the backend deliberately scopes it away from
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:173 (const { data } = useChroniclesSourceState() — isError never read), :186 (data?.data ?? []), :209 (if (!hasAnyBadge) return null → a failed source-state query renders as literally nothing, indistinguishable from no adapters). findings.title: Recent-days index total_minutes sums overlapping episodes across all layers (can exceed 24h/day), diverging from the unioned activity-lane axis the KPI uses

findings.title: Attention items are doors to nowhere: anomaly and open-correction rows carry no action_href even when their evidence surface exists on the same page

findings.title: Duplicate React keys when a day has two or more flagged waking gaps
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:115-123 (adaptAttention: id = `chronicles:${it.kind}:${it.title}`) + editorial.py:775-784 (every gap item shares kind='anomaly', title='Long waking gap', differing only in detail) + AttentionList.tsx:316/337 (key={item.id}). audits.page: /chronicles (ChroniclesPage.tsx + components/chronicles/* + roster/chronicler/api/router.py + src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py). NOTE: task brief said the dev stack was UP, but at audit time (2026-07-18) ports 42200/42173 were not listening and all butlers-dev containers except log-cleanup were in 'Created' state, with the dev DB down — live verification was impossible, so every finding is graded source-confirmed by reading the decisive mechanism. Since the 07-12 baseline the surface gained: timeline trace filter (#3371), stale-mined-routine retirement (#3391), tz-helper extraction (#3420), OwnTracks SSID presence (#3284), Work-lane split (#3216). Known-ledger items re-observed and dropped: ManualRefreshButton still invalidates only byDay/byCategory/dayClose/sourceState/pointEvents keys — none of the briefing/episodes/balance/who/prompts/trends/rollups queries the page now actually renders (ManualRefreshButton.tsx:50-56, unchanged since 07-12); seam error-drop for episodes/pointEvents feeding Scrubber/ribbon/map (ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:113-121); 1904 archive bound; jump-to-date; Gantt keyboard.
audits.jarvis_gap: The chronicles surface is structurally mature — editorial voice column, URL-state day navigation with palette verbs and [ ] t bindings, never-blank placeholder stepping, an IEA drilldown whose new panels (DayNarrative, BalanceRings, WhoYouWereWith, CorrectionPrompts, TrendsLens, WorkScheduleSettings) genuinely honor the SourceDegradedNote convention, honest three-state rollup status, hatched feeder-dark trend bars, and a real correction write-path in the drawer. The gap to JARVIS is concentrated in one theme: the page's most authoritative stratum (headline, state class, voice paragraph, KPI strip) runs on a separate, less honest data spine than the panels below it. The briefing composer never reads the feeder_dark flags its sibling endpoints consume, swallows its own DB failures into calm empties, censors the longest-gap KPI to interior ≥6h gaps, and sums recent-day minutes across overlapping layers — so on a bad-coverage day the top of the page says 'Yesterday was quiet. Nothing needs attention.' while the bottom of the same page hatches lanes as unavailable. Add silent 500-row DESC truncation of dense days, a source-state strip that vanishes on error and shows live-now state on archive days, and attention items with no doors, and the pattern is clear: the evidence layer is honest, the summary layer is trusting. Fixing the summary layer to inherit the evidence layer's honesty is the whole remaining distance to earned calm on this page.
audits.ideal: The ideal /chronicles opens on the most recent settled day and answers 'what was my day, and can I trust this reconstruction?' in five seconds: a voice headline whose state vocabulary includes coverage ('A full day' vs 'Partial record: location was dark 09:00-14:00'), a provenance chip on the prose (llm·cached / templated / stale), and a KPI strip whose numbers share one axis contract with every panel below — unioned activity-lane hours, honest untracked-waking time instead of a censored 'longest gap', sleep with streak. Every attention clause is a door: a gap anomaly focuses that span in the ribbon, unresolved corrections anchor to the corrections panel, a source error deep-links to the connector. The drilldown reconstructs the complete day or says exactly what it is missing — 'showing last 500 of 1,240 points' never happens because the day window is fetched to completion — and the source strip states its time axis ('adapter state as of now') or scopes itself to recent days like the backend already does. Any query failure anywhere on the page names its source inline; nothing renders as a calm empty it cannot prove. Keyboard-first throughout: [ ] t plus jump-to-date, ribbon blocks and drawer fully operable, trend bars click through to their day.

audits.page: /education (EducationPage.tsx + 11 child components; backend roster/education/api/router.py). NOTE: live dev stack was DOWN this run (all butlers-dev containers in "Created" state, nothing listening on 42200/42173, no dev-psql script present) — all evidence is source-confirmed; no live GETs possible.
audits.jarvis_gap: Since the 07-12 baseline nothing shipped on this surface except em-dash copy commits (git log --since=2026-07-12 shows only #3254/#3253), so the baseline knowns remain visibly un-landed in one line: the same 5 of 7 child components still map error to calm (MindMapGraph, ReviewTimeline, MasteryTrendChart, CrossTopicChart, StrugglingNodesCard drop isError), and the pre-Dispatch dialect persists (bg-blue-100/purple-100/sky-100/slate-100/gray-100 badges, border-l-red-500/amber-500/blue-500/gray-300 rails). Beyond those knowns, the deeper gap is that the page is a read-only skin over a system whose lifecycles are all open-ended: the backend already computes the curriculum's true lifecycle (GET /education/flows: pending/diagnosing/planning/teaching/quizzing/reviewing + last_session_at + session_count) but the frontend never calls it, so the page substitutes the unproven "The butler is still building it"; a curriculum request is an invisible LLM-honor-system state lock that can wedge all future requests behind a 409 with no surface, age, or cancel; abandoning a curriculum makes it permanently unreachable in the UI (every list call filters status=active) so the Re-activate control is dead code and the "progress will be preserved" promise is unverifiable; quiz rows carry session_id but render no session door, breaking the signal-to-session-to-evidence spine at its last hop; and review rows are inert divs with no path to the node or to any action. The JARVIS version proves every claim it renders, closes every lifecycle it opens, and puts a door on every number.

findings.title: Teaching-flow lifecycle endpoint exists but the frontend never calls it — page renders unproven 'The butler is still building it' instead of the real build state
findings.evidence: GET /api/education/flows returns per-map status in {pending, diagnosing, planning, teaching, quizzing, reviewing, completed, abandoned} plus session_count, started_at, last_session_at, mastery_pct (roster/education/api/router.py:350-378, models.py:83-92). grep for 'education/flows' and 'TeachingFlow' across frontend/src returns zero hits; frontend/src/api/client.ts:3863-3973 wires every education endpoint EXCEPT /flows and /struggling-nodes. MindMapGraph.tsx:158 renders 'This curriculum has no concepts yet. The butler is still building it.' with no evidence behind the claim. bd open-issue search for curriculum/education/teaching-flow/lifecycle found no bead (only bu-v6uas event-bus and bu-c6wjr background jobs) — the 07-12 'file as a bead' instruction was never executed, so this is re-filed per the ledger's own rule, now with the decisive mechanism: the truth is already served and simply unread.
findings.detail: Failure taxonomy shape 5 (backend-ready, frontend-not-wired). This is the mechanism behind the 07-12 'curriculum dead mid-build 21+ days' incident: a flow stuck in 'diagnosing' with last_session_at 3 weeks old would be instantly visible if /flows were rendered, and a deadman clause (pre-teaching status + last_session_at older than N hours = amber 'build stalled') falls out for free.

findings.title: Curriculum request is an invisible honor-system lock: release depends on the LLM session obeying a prompt step, there is no TTL, no UI surface, and no cancel — a dead session wedges all future requests behind 409 forever
findings.evidence: roster/education/api/router.py:634-773 — POST stores state key pending_curriculum_request (line 745-753) and 409s while it exists (line 737-742). Release paths: (a) the ephemeral LLM session calling state_delete per prompt instruction step 4 (router.py:664-672 — explicitly 'the only case where you leave it set is if teaching_flow_start itself errors'); (b) server-side clear only when the trigger call itself raises (router.py:696-706). A session that spawns then crashes/times out mid-flow leaves the lock set permanently. grep across src/ and roster/ shows no other reader of pending_curriculum_request — no GET exposes it, requested_at is stored (line 750) but never displayed anywhere, and the frontend's only knowledge of the state is the 409 toast (use-education.ts:262-266).
findings.detail: Violates 'every lifecycle closed' and 'failure never impersonates health': a wedged build presents as an eternal benign 'pending'. Owner recovery requires knowing the state-store key name and using the generic state admin surface. Fix shape: promote to a visible request lifecycle (requested → started → failed with age) + TTL/watchdog + cancel door on the page.

findings.title: Abandoned and completed curricula are unreachable anywhere in the UI; the Re-activate control is dead code and the 'progress will be preserved' promise is unverifiable
findings.evidence: Every useMindMaps caller hardcodes {status:'active'}: EducationPage.tsx:26, ReviewTimeline.tsx:66, ButlerEducationReviewsTab.tsx:87. CurriculumActions.tsx:63-71 renders 'Re-activate' only when status==='abandoned' — a value no map in any rendered list can carry, so the branch is unreachable (taxonomy shape 12 unreachable-branch + shape 7 orphan). The abandon confirm dialog (CurriculumActions.tsx:80-84) promises 'Your progress will be preserved but the butler will stop scheduling reviews' — after confirm + invalidate, the map disappears from the selector with no route back. Backend supports listing by any status (router.py:152-163, _VALID_STATUSES active/completed/abandoned at router.py:588).
findings.detail: Secondary bug in the same path: after abandon succeeds, selectedMapId still points at the delisted map; the auto-select effect (EducationPage.tsx:35-39) only fires when !selectedMapId, so the Select renders blank while MindMapGraph continues showing the abandoned map via the by-id detail fetch (useMindMap still enabled) — a half-ghost state.

findings.title: Quiz responses carry session_id but render no session door — trace spine (signal → session → evidence) broken at the last hop
findings.evidence: QuizResponse.session_id exists in the FE type (frontend/src/api/types.ts:4038) and API model (roster/education/api/models.py:66), but QuizHistoryList.tsx renders question, quality, answer, evaluator_notes and never session_id — no `/sessions/${id}` link, while sibling surfaces have the door pattern (frontend/src/components/qa/SessionDoors.tsx, costs/TopSessionsTable.tsx). The expanded row shows the evaluator's verdict with no way to open the session that produced it. (bu-vyjoi covers DispatchVerdict openers on ingestion/issues/calendar/butler-detail — education quiz rows are not in its scope.)

findings.title: Review rows are drill-down dead ends: inert divs with no door to the node, the curriculum, or any action
findings.evidence: ReviewTimeline.tsx:40-63 — ReviewEntryRow is a plain div (no onClick, no link); it shows label + map title + a date but clicking does nothing. Node detail exists only in the Curriculum tab (EducationPage.tsx:161-165) and nothing connects a due review to it. The Detect→Diagnose→Act loop (docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md, 'three critical loops') dies at Detect: an 'Overdue' group renders and the operator can neither inspect the node nor trigger a review session from the console.

findings.evidence: ReviewTimeline.tsx:33 buckets via classifyReviewBucket(entry.next_review_at, now, tz, ...) using the owner tz from useTimezone (line 78), but the rendered date at ReviewTimeline.tsx:58 is raw `new Date(entry.next_review_at).toLocaleDateString()` (host tz); QuizHistoryList.tsx also uses toLocaleDateString for responded_at, while NodeDetailPanel.tsx correctly uses the shared <Time> component (mode=absolute). Same class of defect the 07-12 epic fixed for sessions (owner-tz date filters), new instance on education.

findings.title: CrossTopicChart and StrugglingNodesCard return null on empty (and on error, per the known) — features that vanish teach nothing and are indistinguishable from not existing
findings.evidence: CrossTopicChart.tsx:16 `if (!analytics || analytics.topics.length === 0) return null;`; StrugglingNodesCard.tsx:24 `if (!mindMapId || struggling.length === 0) return null;`. A healthy system with no struggling nodes renders nothing rather than an earned-calm 'No struggling concepts — all reviews on track', and a new owner never learns these panels exist (discoverability bias 7; distinct from the 5-of-7 error→calm known, which is about isError — this is the empty branch).

findings.title: Analytics numbers wear current-data authority with no as-of signal
findings.evidence: MasterySummaryCards.tsx renders Avg Mastery / Est. Completion with no snapshot timestamp; the backend serves snapshot_date and created_at (models.py:72-80) but neither is rendered outside the trend chart's x-axis. If the daily snapshot job dies, day-old (or week-old) numbers render identically to fresh ones — no freshness plaque or deadman, in contrast to the 07-12 health freshness spine. Overlaps partially with open bu-c6wjr (durable health surface for background jobs) on the producer side; the missing FE as-of plaque is not covered there.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade education surface is a learning-operations console where nothing renders that the system cannot prove: each curriculum wears its true lifecycle as a first-class plaque (diagnosing / teaching / reviewing, sourced from the teaching-flow state machine, with last-session age and a deadman that turns amber the moment a build stalls), curriculum requests are visible closable lifecycles (pending with age, started, failed-with-reason, cancellable) instead of an invisible lock, and the full portfolio — active, completed, abandoned — is browsable so abandonment is a reversible door, not an oubliette. Reviews open first as the hot loop: each due item is a door (Enter opens the node dossier; a keyboard-driven action triggers a review session or nudges the butler), every mastery number and quiz verdict carries a one-click door to the exact session that produced it, all dates render in owner time via the shared Time component, analytics carry an as-of plaque, and every panel speaks pure Dispatch — status vars only, honest error states on all seven children, earned-calm empty states that teach what the panel will show.

moves.why: 'Failure never impersonates health; staleness never wears current-data authority' (north star) and purpose-and-single-pane's Detect loop — the owner's only curriculum sat dead mid-build 21+ days behind 'still building it' while the backend already served status=diagnosing + last_session_at. findings.title: All notification provenance since 2026-05-01 is double-encoded jsonb and silently nulled by the API
findings.detail: log_notification() pre-serializes metadata with json.dumps before binding, and the pool-level jsonb codec json.dumps it AGAIN, so every row written since the codec cutover stores a jsonb STRING scalar instead of an object. The API's _normalize_notification_metadata then sees a str (not a Mapping) and returns None. Net effect: 588/793 rows (every row from 2026-05-01 through today) carry rich provenance in the DB — request_context.request_id, origin (e.g. model_breaker_monitor), catalog_entry_id, the full notify.v1 envelope — and the dashboard receives metadata:null for all of them. 499 of those rows contain a request_context door the UI could open. The docstring's 'legacy rows may contain non-object JSON' has reality inverted: the NEW rows are the corrupted ones. Fix is three-part: stop the double-dump at the write site, unwrap string-scalar rows at read time ((metadata #>> '{}')::jsonb backfill), and actually render/door the provenance.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/notification/log.py:76 (json.dumps(metadata or {})) + src/butlers/db.py:137-143 (_jsonb_encoder json.dumps again, registered db.py:170-176); src/butlers/api/routers/notifications.py:58-70 (non-Mapping → None); live SQL: jsonb_typeof(metadata) → string=588 (2026-05-01→2026-07-16), object=205 (2026-03-27→2026-05-01); 499 string rows contain request_context; live GET /api/notifications returns "metadata":null for row e41646b8 whose DB value holds origin+catalog_entry_id

findings.title: The entire 'Retried' vocabulary is dead against live data — a filter option that can never match
findings.detail: effective_status='retried' and the ?status=retried filter both require session_id IS NOT NULL (_RETRIED_EXISTS_SQL), and session_id is never written (finding #2). Live: ?status=retried returns total=0 all-time; raw failed (87) equals terminal failed (87) because the NOT-EXISTS exclusion in /stats can never fire. So the status dropdown offers 'Retried' (bu-5gf99 added it deliberately), the feed has an amber Retried badge, and the stats endpoint runs its most expensive self-join query — all for a state that is structurally unreachable. The UI implies a retry-supersession axis the system never populates. Either stamp session_id so supersession can match, or remove the vocabulary (zero-cruft bar).

findings.title: 'Until' date filter silently excludes the entire chosen day (exclusive UTC midnight, no owner-tz) — the sessions fix (bu-hmdqz.12) never reached notifications

findings.title: Failed critical alerts offer no recovery verb — ack/bury is the only action, live instance: the 'WhatsApp unlinked, ingestion paused' alert never reached the owner and can only be marked read

audits.page: /notifications (NotificationsPage.tsx + notification-feed/stats-bar/verdict-opener + /api/notifications router)
audits.jarvis_gap: The page chrome is genuinely good — URL-backed filters, j/k/a triage with advertised bindings, degraded envelopes on both list and stats, a windowed DispatchVerdict opener, never-blank refetches. But underneath, the trace spine this surface exists to expose is 100% severed: not one of 793 rows carries session_id/trace_id, so the Session/Trace doors are code that has never rendered, the 'Retried' filter/badge/stats-exclusion is vocabulary for an unreachable state (?status=retried → 0 all-time), and since 2026-05-01 every row's provenance (request_id, origin, catalog_entry_id, the full notify envelope) is double-encoded at write time and nulled by the API before the UI could ever show it. The owner is reading a delivery log that renders machine chat-ids as recipients, cannot open any notification to its cause, silently drops the final day from 'Until' filters, and whose only verb on a failed critical alert — including a live 'WhatsApp ingestion paused' alert that never reached the owner — is to mark it read. It looks like earned calm; it is a well-dressed table over a provenance pipeline that destroys its own evidence.
audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade notifications surface is the fleet's outbound-delivery ledger with an unbroken spine: it opens with a windowed verdict whose every clause deep-links to the exact predicate it claims (window included), tiles and list share one 'failed' definition, and each row is a door — recipient resolved to a contact name, origin resolved to its producer (session, connector incident, breaker event, or scheduled job) via the stamped session_id/trace_id/request_id, one keystroke from row to root evidence. Failure is a workflow, not a stain: a failed row shows why it failed, offers Retry (re-invoking deliver from the stored notify.v1 envelope, with owner-contact fallback for missing recipients) and records the attempt lineage so 'retried' is a real, reachable state; acknowledgment is an immutable acked_at overlay that never rewrites delivery history. Filters are owner-tz inclusive, the butler filter is a picker not a spelling test, and every count the page shows is one the system can prove from the rows beneath it.

audits.page: /system (SystemPage.tsx + components/system/* tiles, SystemVerdictBanner, TopologyGraph; backend src/butlers/api/routers/system.py). NOTE: live verification was impossible this run — the dev stack is DOWN (butlers-dev-migrations-1 Exited(1) "Migration failed for: chronicler" ~3h before audit; all app containers stuck in Created; 127.0.0.1:42200 connection refused). audits.jarvis_gap: Today /system opens with a genuinely good judgment layer (SystemVerdictBanner: ranked problems, no premature all-clear, honest degraded envelopes for drift/deploy/backups) and every tile has real loading/error/empty/degraded states — the bones are the best on the dashboard. But the verdict's court is incomplete and its calm is not fully earned: the banner unions only 7 of the page's 10 data sources, so "Instance healthy" can render directly above an erroring Data Egress or Database Size tile; and its fleet input masks settled errors whenever any cached payload exists (isError && !data), so a dead /api/butlers/board keeps asserting "all N beating" from an arbitrarily old snapshot with no age signal — stale data wearing current-data authority at the single most authoritative pixel on the page. Failure signals dead-end: "N insights failed to deliver" is a number with no door to the failed candidates, breaking the signal→session→evidence spine exactly on the failure branch. Two same-page answers to "when did we last deploy" can disagree (VersionTile's process-start proxy vs the real deployments ledger one card away), an orphaned heartbeat endpoint+hook survives with zero consumers, and the egress tile's "Owner only" 403 branch is unreachable theater. Versus the ideal, the page verifies the fleet in five seconds when everything works, but its verdict cannot yet be trusted to be the last word when its own inputs rot or fail.
audits.ideal: The ideal /system is the instance's single sworn statement: one verdict line computed from the union of every source rendered anywhere on the page (fleet board, instance, backups, insights, posture, drift, deployments, database, egress, connectors), stamped with its own freshness ("as of 12s ago") and constitutionally incapable of asserting all-clear from stale or partially failed inputs — a source that stops answering degrades the verdict within one poll interval, visibly. Every problem line is a door: fleet problems to /butlers, backup/drift/deploy problems anchor-scroll to their evidence tile, failed insights open the actual failed candidate rows with their delivery-attempt trail and originating session. Software identity is one card with one truth — serving SHA, version, commits-behind, deployed-at from the deployments ledger, process uptime as a clearly-subordinate fact — not three cards with two contradictory "last deploy" claims. Below the verdict, a 24h instance timeline (deploys, drift onset/clear, backup events, butler offline episodes) turns the page from a snapshot into a flight recorder, keyboard-walkable, every event a door.

findings.title: Stale fleet data wears current-data authority: board errors are masked whenever a cached payload exists, so a dead board API keeps the verdict saying 'all N beating' indefinitely
findings.detail: useButlerStatusBoard defines aggregates.isError as `boardQuery.isError && !boardQuery.data`. In TanStack v5 a settled background-refetch failure sets status='error' while retaining the last successful data — so once any payload has ever loaded, a permanently failing GET /api/butlers/board never re-surfaces as an error. SystemVerdictBanner then sees board.isError=false and keeps computing offline/quarantined/overdue (and the 'all N beating' all-clear) from an arbitrarily old snapshot, with no age signal anywhere on the banner. ButlerHeartbeatTile shares the same masked flag. The sibling per-tile hooks (useInstanceFacts etc.) use plain isError and DO flip to error state, so the page's most authoritative element has strictly weaker failure honesty than its trivia tiles. Distinct from the fenced taxonomy-11 case (single-source aggregate derivation) — this is deliberate error suppression conditioned on cache.

findings.title: Egress tile's 'Owner only' 403 state is structurally unreachable — the gate checks that an owner EXISTS, not who is calling

audits.page: /timeline (TimelinePage.tsx + TimelineLedger/TimelineEventDrawer/NewEventsPill, use-timeline-ledger, api/routers/timeline.py)
audits.jarvis_gap: Mechanically this surface is near the top of the fleet: URL-backed filters/views/drawer, a real live tail with an honest pinned/committed snapshot model, per-source degraded meta, a wall-clock-decaying Live badge with a distinct Down state, server-side heartbeat classification, and the just-landed errors lens verified working live (23 failed sessions + 27 failed deliveries under event_type=error). But walked as the owner, the headline promise — "Every household event, newest first" — fails at first glance on live data: ~90% of the head page (179/200 events over 3.7h) is one butler's internal memory-consolidation sessions, each dumping its raw system prompt ("# Memory Consolidation You are performing memory consolidation for the butler ecosystem...") into the serif human-intent column. The owner's 13 real events (routed messages, calendar fires) are buried under machine maintenance the heartbeat collapse doesn't cover. The five-second-verification north star inverts: five seconds on this page teaches "the system is grinding on itself," not "the household is fine." Secondary honesty gaps (butler facet errors render as calm "No butlers available", Load-older fails silently, degraded banner can't name which butler's history is missing) and a zero-keyboard hot loop (no palette verbs, no j/k — 13 sibling pages register commands, this one registers none) keep it below the bar the rest of its own architecture sets.
audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade chronicle is the household's diary, not the fleet's process log: it opens with only owner-meaningful events — messages routed, decisions made, notifications delivered, calendar fires, failures — every row written in human language because no raw machine prompt can ever reach the summary column (labels are derived from structured trigger metadata by default; free text renders only when it is provably the human's own words). Machine metabolism (heartbeats, consolidation, backfills, QA canaries) collapses into one quiet rollup line per hour — "travel: 8 maintenance runs, all green" — expandable on demand and toggleable as an Internal lens, so a runaway job reads as an anomaly plaque ("travel has run consolidation 48×/hr for 4h — investigate") instead of wallpaper. Every row is a door on the trace spine: sessions land on the transcript, notifications land on the exact delivery record, and every failure names itself. The whole loop is keyboard-first — j/k to walk rows, Enter to peek, e for the Errors lens, . to jump to now, palette verbs for save/clear view — and every data source that feeds the page (butlers list, older pages, per-butler session fan-out) either proves itself or names its failure inline with a retry.

findings.title: 97 approved-but-never-dispatched actions are invisible: the stalled-action radar sees only the last-30-decided keyhole
findings.evidence: Live dev DB (stack API was down; migrations container exited 1, so SQL + static trace substitute): relationship.pending_actions has 97 rows status='approved' (owner-approved via dashboard, never executed) spanning 2026-05-23 → 2026-07-16, including 4 `notify` outbound messages and 50 entity_merge; yet the top-30 decided rows across all pools (ORDER BY decided_at DESC LIMIT 30, src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1681-1741, _WAITING_STATUSES={'pending'} at :1595 so 'approved' lives only in history) are ALL status='executed' (messenger executes constantly). The verdict opener derives its 'N stalled actions never ran' clause solely from those 30 rows (frontend/src/components/approvals/approvals-verdict-opener.tsx:74-87), and HistorySection fetches getApprovalsHistory(undefined, 30) (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1099) — the only place the Retry affordance exists (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1151-1153). Net: opener shows a calm '4 waiting', zero stalled clause, zero reachable retry, for 97 authorized side-effects that silently never ran.
findings.detail: This defeats the exact mechanism the 07-12 'amber stalled, never success-green' doctrine built: the vocabulary is honest but the window is a keyhole. The approve toast even says 'Retry from History' (use-approval-decisions.ts:162) — but a busy executed stream permanently evicts stalled rows from that history. No backend endpoint exposes a stalled count or stalled-only filter (flat list state=waiting|decided|all only, approvals.py:1626). Failure impersonating health on the Trust Console itself.

findings.title: Command-palette 'Approve next' bypasses the undo-window contract and the double-decision guard
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1567-1578 — perform: () => approveMut.mutate(effectiveSelected) fires the raw mutation instantly, while the keyboard 'a' verb routes through scheduleDecision + UNDO_WINDOW_MS (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1510-1515, use-approval-decisions.ts:201-221). The palette entry displays binding ['a'] (display-only metadata per command-registry.tsx:45-53), advertising parity with the undoable key. It also never consults scheduledDecisions, the guard the Dossier explicitly exists to enforce (ApprovalsPage.tsx:479-484).
findings.detail: Failure scenario: owner presses 'd' on the selected item (deny scheduled, 5s undo), then opens the palette and runs 'Approve next' — approve fires immediately, then the scheduled deny fires 5s later against an already-approved action (409/conflicting decision), or vice versa. Also mislabeled: it approves the currently-routed item (effectiveSelected honors the URL :id), not 'next'. This is the only remaining irreversible approve path after bu-qvnce.4 unified everything else onto the grace window.

findings.title: Decided dossier omits the decision outcome: decided_by/decided_at never rendered (a code comment claims they are), deny reason and execution_result unreachable
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1138-1141 comment: 'the Dossier pane already renders a decided state (no decision cluster, decided_by/decided_at shown)' — but grep of ApprovalsPage.tsx/components/approvals finds zero render sites for decided_by/decided_at; the Dossier shows only the status word (ApprovalsPage.tsx:679-683). Backend serves both fields (approvals.py:368-369; models/approval.py:105-106) and the FE type carries them (frontend/src/api/types.ts:3015-3016). Deny reason is stuffed into decided_by ('recorded in decided_by', src/butlers/modules/approvals/operations.py:328) and execution_result exists only on ApprovalAction (types.ts:2946), absent from ApprovalDetail entirely (models/approval.py:85-115) — so an executed dossier cannot show what ran and a stalled dossier cannot show why dispatch failed.
findings.detail: Every history row is a door to /approvals/:id 'for auditability', but the audit trail ends at a bare status label: who decided (owner vs telegram callback vs auto-rule), when, with what reason, and with what execution outcome are all missing. The trace spine (signal → session → evidence) has its final link cut at the decided end. Note possible adjacency to the 07-12 known 'carry decision substance through the door' — that known's fields (why/evidence/blast_radius/reversibility, #3383) DID land and render; this finding is specifically the decision-outcome fields plus a comment asserting behavior the code does not have.

findings.title: Autonomy-suggestion, rule-promotion, and promotion-stats sections drop isError — a failed fetch renders as calm absence
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1180 `const { data } = useAutonomySuggestions(...)` and :1196 `if (suggestions.length === 0) return null` — isError never read; identically RulePromotionSection :1225-1244; RulePromotionStatsSection :1287-1302 returns null when `!stats` (hard query error → data undefined), despite its own docstring claiming it renders 'whenever a source is degraded (so a failed query surfaces instead of the section silently vanishing)' — that only covers meta.sources_degraded with data present, not a failed request.
findings.detail: New instances of systemic sin #2 (error impersonating calm empty) on a page that otherwise handles this best-in-fleet (queueDegradedNote, opener degraded clauses). A 500 on /suggestions means pending autonomy-boundary changes silently vanish with no tell anywhere — the sections' conditional-render-on-content design makes error and genuine-absence pixel-identical.

findings.title: Dossier fetch failure is a dead-end: no retry, no cause, not the fleet's degraded vocabulary
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:470-476 — `if (error || !data?.data)` renders a bare muted 'failed to load dossier' with no retry affordance, no error detail, no 404 (approval gone) vs network distinction, while the same file imports and uses QueryBoundary/SourceDegradedNote everywhere else (:76, :1620, :1109).
findings.detail: This is the landing pane for every deep link (Telegram push, history row, verdict-opener clause, bookmark). A transient API blip on arrival strands the owner one refetch away from the decision with no button to press; recovery requires a full page reload.

findings.title: The stalled dossier offers no Retry — the recovery verb lives only on the history list row, and the verdict opener doors past it
findings.evidence: Retry dispatch is rendered only inside HistorySection rows for status==='approved' (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1151-1153); the Dossier renders no action cluster at all when status !== 'pending' (isPending gate at :479, :495). The opener's 'one stalled action never ran' clause links to `/approvals/${id}` (approvals-verdict-opener.tsx:79) — a dossier where the advertised recovery action does not exist.
findings.detail: Walkthrough failure (Recovery step): the system names the failure, doors you to the item, then makes you go back and hunt the matching row in a 30-item list to act. Compounds the critical keyhole finding: even when a stalled action IS visible, its detail door drops the verb.

findings.title: Expiry countdowns and urgency ranking freeze between refetches — 'expires in 3m' can read 3m for 5 minutes
findings.evidence: expiryCountdown/rankScore call Date.now() at render only (ApprovalsPage.tsx:191-225); rankedPending memo depends solely on [data] (:1363-1366); the reconciliation poll is POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS = 5min (frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:23) and bus events fire only on state transitions, not time passage. No interval re-render exists on the page.
findings.detail: Sub-hour countdowns (the red-warn <=1h band, :217) are precisely the ones that go stale-wearing-current between polls; an item can silently cross into 'expired' with the chip still promising minutes, and the expiry-dominated rank order (:203-207) doesn't re-sort as urgency bands shift. Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-12 'poll cadence' known — this is client-side clock ticking, fixable without any network change.

findings.title: /decisions never refreshes while open — no poll, no bus producer, and the as-of plaque's age freezes too
findings.evidence: useDecisions has no refetchInterval (frontend/src/hooks/use-decisions.ts:13-18) and beads-export changes emit no fleet-bus event (digest is a bind-mounted JSONL read, src/butlers/api/routers/decisions.py:4-11); formatExportAsOf/resolveExportAsOfIsWarn compute age at render only (DecisionsPage.tsx:59-85), so 'export as of 3h ago' and its 48h warn tint never advance without a remount/window-focus.
findings.detail: The page shipped an honest staleness plaque (bu-hmdqz.6) but the plaque itself stales: an owner who keeps the Decisions tab open sees a snapshot with an age caption that stops counting. One refetchInterval (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS is the fleet token for exactly this bus-less case) plus a ticking now closes it. Decision actions/one-tap close are fenced (bu-ckkpz); refresh cadence is not.

findings.title: One-line fenced observation: dossier blast_radius/reversibility columns are live but unpopulated (0 of 1,288 rows on dev)
findings.evidence: Live dev DB: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE blast_radius IS NOT NULL) FROM relationship.pending_actions → 0/1288; FE 'Decision impact' therefore reads 'Not classified'/'Not classified' universally (ApprovalsPage.tsx:730-740) and the declared-radius ranking path (:185) is dead, falling back to the tool-name regex. Population is bu-24lu6 in-flight scope — noted, not filed.
findings.detail: Reported per instructions as a one-line un-landed observation only; the columns/plumbing (#3383) are real and correctly consumed once writers populate them.

audits.page: approvals-decisions (/approvals, /approvals/:id, /decisions)
audits.ideal: The Trust Console is the one room where the owner's authority over the fleet is exercised and audited, and every state an approval can occupy — waiting, scheduled-with-undo, stalled, executed, denied, expired — is a first-class, countable, actionable citizen. The opener verdict is computed from whole-population counts (never a list-window), so '97 stalled actions never ran, oldest 56d' is impossible to miss and doors into a dedicated stalled lane with retry/abandon verbs, bulk retry, and per-item dispatch-failure cause. Every dossier is a complete decision record: rationale and typed evidence before deciding; who/when/why/with-what-execution-result after — one unbroken trace from Telegram push or history row through session to outcome, with the recovery verb present wherever the failure is named. Every actuation path (click, keyboard, palette, dashboard row, Telegram tap) rides one identical undo-window contract; countdowns tick in real time and re-rank as urgency bands shift; every conditional section renders its failure as loudly as its content. /decisions matures from a read-only title-marker digest into the same shape — structured options, defaults, deadlines, one-tap close — until the two surfaces are simply two lanes of one 'what needs Tze' room that refreshes itself and never wears a stale age caption.
audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-12 work made this the fleet's most honest surface in vocabulary — amber 'stalled' never renders success-green, degraded fan-outs are named, empties are classified, the undo-window is a shared contract, keyboard triage is best-in-product. But the honesty is window-scoped, not population-scoped: the stalled-action radar only sees the last 30 decided rows, and on the live data plane those are 100% executed rows, so 97 owner-approved actions that never ran (including 4 outbound notify messages) produce zero pixels anywhere — the exact failure-impersonates-health shape the surface was rebuilt to kill, reintroduced by a LIMIT 30. Downstream of that: the recovery verb (Retry) exists only on history list rows, the dossier for a decided action is an audit door with the audit trail missing (no decided_by/decided_at/reason/execution_result, despite a comment claiming otherwise), and one actuation path (palette Approve) still bypasses the undo contract every other path shares. The five-second verification test currently passes only when the system is genuinely healthy; when it is quietly failing to dispatch, the console reads calm. Closing the keyhole, completing the dossier's outcome half, and unifying the last actuation path would take this surface from 'honest about what it looks at' to 'honest about everything that exists' — the actual JARVIS bar.

moves.title: Stalled-actions lane: whole-population radar + retry/abandon verbs
moves.why: Doctrine: 'failure never impersonates health' and five-second fleet verification (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md; purpose-and-single-pane.md). Live dev data shows 97 approved-never-dispatched actions with zero pixels: the opener's stalled clause and the only Retry affordance both live inside a 30-row decided window saturated by executed rows (approvals.py:1681-1741; approvals-verdict-opener.tsx:74-87; ApprovalsPage.tsx:1151). Owner payoff: authorized side-effects can no longer silently not-happen.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: add stalled support to the flat endpoint (state=stalled → status='approved') plus a cheap COUNT per pool surfaced in meta (or a /api/approvals/stalled-summary), degraded-tracked like the existing fan-outs. 2) Opener: derive the stalled clause from the count, not the 30-row history slice; clause doors to the stalled lane. 3) UI: stalled section (or rail filter) with per-row Retry, an 'abandon' verb (terminal state so ancient stalled rows can be retired deliberately), and bulk retry; age shown per row. 4) Dossier for status='approved' gains the same Retry/abandon cluster (kills the opener-doors-to-a-dossier-without-the-verb dead end).
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py (flat/history endpoints, DegradedSources), frontend/src/components/approvals/approvals-verdict-opener.tsx, ApprovalsPage.tsx HistorySection/Dossier, use-approval-decisions.ts (retry mutation joins the shared cache-reconcile keys), event-cache-registry approvalPatch.

moves.why: Trace-spine doctrine: every clause a door on an unbroken signal→session→evidence chain. The decided dossier currently ends at a bare status word; decided_by/decided_at are served but never rendered (comment at ApprovalsPage.tsx:1138-1141 falsely claims they are), deny reason is stuffed into decided_by (operations.py:328), and execution_result is absent from ApprovalDetail entirely (models/approval.py:85-115). Owner payoff: 'who decided this, when, and what actually happened' answered in the dossier itself, including WHY a stalled dispatch failed.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: add execution_result + a first-class denial_reason to ApprovalDetail (stop overloading decided_by; backward compat waived — split the column semantics). 2) FE: 'Decision' section on non-pending dossiers — actor (owner@telegram vs dashboard vs auto:rule with door to the rule), decided_at, reason, and for executed/stalled the execution result or dispatch error verbatim. 3) Fix or delete the lying comment; add a decided-dossier render test asserting the outcome fields appear.

AutonomySuggestionsSection/RulePromotionSection drop isError entirely and RulePromotionStatsSection returns null on hard error despite its docstring (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1180-1196, 1225-1244, 1287-1302); the Dossier's own failure is a retry-less dead end (:470-476). moves.why: Doctrine: staleness never wears current-data authority. The decisions digest has no bus producer (bind-mounted JSONL read, decisions.py:4-11) and useDecisions has no refetchInterval (use-decisions.ts:13-18) — the lane is a mount-time snapshot. The fenced bu-ckkpz scope is actions/options, not refresh cadence. Owner payoff: the decision lane and its sidebar badge stay current without tab-cycling.

audits.page: butler-detail (/butlers/:name) — ButlerDetailPage.tsx + components/butler-detail/* (header, actions, overview, activity/system sections, sibling nav)
audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-12 "one console, one tab set" restructure (bu-86c4c.18) genuinely landed: single tab vocabulary with 1-9/[/] shortcuts in lockstep with the rail, unified prompt-first command bar that door-links straight to the spawned session, quarantine reason surfaced at the Resume decision point, stripe bars and event rows as doors, and a disciplined pending-decision state machine on inline approvals (f23ca9030). What lags is the honesty last-mile: the flagship header identity line currently tells the owner finance's "next" run was 67 days ago (stale past next_run_at rendered with upcoming-run authority); the Recent panel prints raw "REQUEST CONTEXT {json..." routed-message envelopes as event summaries even though the unwrap machinery already exists in timeline.py; the board API computes per-row degraded flags (stripe_source_error, schema_unreachable) that the Overview drops on the floor, rendering a calm all-zero stripe during an outage; header ("--") and Overview ("$0.00") give two different simultaneous answers for the same spend-today quantity; and the sibling nav's error state is an eternal skeleton that kills fleet navigation. Known-ledger residue still visible un-landed (one line each): the Overview "review" door still emits dead ?butler=&id= params even though /approvals/:id now exists; the detail endpoint's "online" status vocabulary still renders a dim/gray dot for a healthy butler (parallel status vocabulary). Ideal: a console where every rendered fact is provable, freshness-stamped, and a door — today it is a well-shaped console whose facts are ~85% provable and ~50% doors.
audits.ideal: The butler console opens on a provable now: an identity line whose three facts — last run, next fire, spend today — are each sourced, freshness-honest, and doors (last run opens that session, next opens the schedule row, spend opens the Spend tab); an enabled schedule whose fire time has passed renders as an explicit overdue signal, never as a "next" fact. Every Overview number is either live-verified or visibly degraded using the flags the board already computes — an unreachable schema shows a degraded stripe pixel and an "unknown" KPI tone, never a calm zero. Recent events read as human language distilled from the trace spine (the same display_summary the timeline uses), each one hop from its session transcript. Butler-scoped approvals speak the same j/k/a/d triage vocabulary as the global Approvals desk, and the review door lands on /approvals/:id. One filled-primary action (Run); Pause is a guarded outline secondary. Sibling navigation never dies with the board query — the roster is static knowledge and stays navigable with an honest "status unknown" badge. Every KPI panel is a one-keystroke door, so signal→evidence is never a re-find through the tab rail.

findings.title: Header 'next' fact renders a 67-day-old timestamp as the upcoming run
findings.detail: earliestNextRun() filters only on `s.enabled && s.next_run_at` and takes the earliest — it never filters to the future. Finance has two enabled one-shot calendar-sourced schedules ('IBKR SPCE Class Action Filing Deadline'/'Recovery') with next_run_at 2026-05-11/2026-05-16, so the header identity line renders "next 67d ago" (Time relative-compact suffixes past deltas with ' ago'). Relationship has the same with 'SUTD Homecoming 2026 registration' (past by a day). Staleness wearing current-data authority on the single most-glanced line of the page; two layers: the scheduler leaves stale next_run_at on enabled already-fired schedules (backend), and the header renders any past value as 'next' (frontend).
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:59-67 (earliestNextRun, no future filter), :186 (renders 'next' + Time relative-compact); live GET /api/butlers/finance/schedules → enabled=true, next_run_at=2026-05-11T14:54:48Z; Time semantics frontend/src/components/ui/time.tsx:16-18 (past → 'Nd ago')

findings.title: Recent-activity feed prints raw routed-message envelopes as event summaries
findings.detail: activity_feed.py builds session_completed summaries as a bare prompt[:120] truncation, so the butler-detail Recent panel shows 'REQUEST CONTEXT (for reply targeting and audit traceability):\n{\n "request_id": ...' as the human summary of a session (live on finance, 2 of 5 events). memory_write summaries are likewise session narration ('No concrete event to act on. Exiting silently.') rather than what was remembered. timeline.py already carries the exact unwrap machinery for this (routed_message/user_message fence extraction + REQUEST CONTEXT preamble stripping, built for the 07-12 'timeline summary unwrap' landing) — the activity-feed endpoint never adopted it, so the same session reads as human text on the timeline and machine plumbing on butler detail (one-vocabulary violation).

findings.title: Overview stripe and sessions KPI drop the board's per-row degraded flags — fabricated calm during outages
findings.detail: The board hook exposes row.hourlyStripeError (schema_unreachable || stripe_source_error) and heartbeatUnavailable per row, plus fleet-level sessionsSourceError — the exact honest fan-out flags the fleet convention (bu-qvnce.1) mandates consuming. ButlerOverviewTab ignores all of them: stripe falls back to Array(24).fill(0) (24 calm quiet bars with real-data authority) and sessions24h falls back through to a confident 0. A butler whose schema was unreachable when the board was computed renders as a peacefully idle butler. (The spend `?? 0` sibling on line 351 is 07-12-ledgered — excluded; this is the stripe/sessions instance, which has the flags available in the same row object and drops them.)

Array(24).fill(0)), :350 (sessions24h ?? 0), no reference to hourlyStripeError anywhere in the file; flags defined frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:169 (hourlyStripeError), :124-127 (sessionsSourceError contract: 'NOT a confident fleet-wide total')

Beyond the ledgered ??0-honesty issue, this is a one-instrument consistency defect (two renderings of one quantity disagree), and '--' also conflates 'genuinely spent nothing' with 'unknown'.

The action bar thus presents two competing filled primaries, and the persistent one is the riskier action (quarantines the butler fleet-wide via the registry eligibility API, single un-confirmed click). Reversibility makes no-confirm acceptable, but the visual hierarchy is inverted: Run is the hot-loop primary; Pause should be outline/secondary.

findings.detail: The sessions (24h), spend (today), and awaiting panels each display a count whose evidence lives one obvious hop away (?tab=activity&section=sessions, ?tab=spend, ?tab=approvals) but none is clickable — only the stripe bars, event rows, and the (dead-params, ledgered) review link are doors. The awaiting KPI correctly shows meta.total (can exceed the 5-row preview) yet offers no 'view all N' door, so signal→evidence requires re-finding through the tab rail. Config panel counts (modules/schedules/skills) similarly don't open their System sections.

findings.title: Butler-scoped approvals have no keyboard triage path

findings.title: Chat — the flagship JARVIS surface — is completely silent to screen readers
findings.detail: MessageThread, ChatPanel, TypingIndicator, and FloatingChatWidget contain no aria-live region, no role='log'/'status', and no aria-busy anywhere. A screen-reader user sends a message and receives no announcement when the assistant reply streams in, when streaming completes, when the typing indicator appears, or when a reply arrives while the widget is closed (the unread state only changes the launcher's aria-label, perceivable only by re-focusing it). TypingIndicator is three bouncing div dots with no text alternative at all. The 'talk to your butler' loop — the core JARVIS interaction — is unusable without sight. Buttons in the widget are well-labeled; the conversation itself is the gap.

audits.page: cross:accessibility (whole-frontend sweep: secrets passport, chat widget, entity/relationship pages, education, settings/models, charts across dashboard/spend/health/education/ingestion, shell/sidebar, axe+lint infrastructure)
audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS you cannot hear and cannot feel: the flagship chat loop is completely silent to assistive tech (no live region anywhere in the thread — a blind owner literally never hears the butler answer), keyboard focus vanishes exactly where trust matters most (credential-entry fields on the Secrets Passport), and the WHY behind model failures lives only under a mouse hover. The primitives layer (lint gate, reduced-motion floor, modal choreography, StateDot) is genuinely strong now — but the CI safety net only audits empty pages, so every populated-state regression ships invisibly. Earned calm requires every state change to be perceivable without sight or pointer; today perceivability is a property of the loading state.
audits.ideal: Perceivability as an enforced invariant, not a per-surface courtesy. Four floors, each with a mechanism that makes the next regression impossible: (1) a global :focus-visible ring in index.css that no surface can silently opt out of, plus a lint ban on outline-none without a focus-visible replacement; (2) one announcement primitive (role='log' thread + shared useAnnounce/LiveRegion) through which chat streaming, optimistic mutations, and background refetches all speak; (3) the axe route sweep extended to fixture-populated states with color-contrast re-enabled, so 'covered route' means covered as the owner actually sees it; (4) shared accessible wrappers for the two chronically re-solved widgets — ChartFrame (aria summary + accessibilityLayer + table fallback, lint-enforced on recharts imports) and a focusable Hint primitive replacing raw title=. With those four, WCAG 2.2 AA stops being an audit outcome and becomes a build-time property — the same move the repo already made for design tokens and poll policy.

findings.title: Memory search renders the verified-empty verdict "Nothing in the books." while the query is still loading
findings.detail: SearchResults destructures only {data, isError, refetch} from useMemoryInspect — there is no isLoading branch at all. On first submit (and on every kind-pill switch, which changes the query key), data is undefined, results=[] falls through the isError guard, and the component renders the serif-italic empty verdict for the full fetch duration, then results pop in. A pending state impersonates a truthful no-match verdict — the exact 'fabricated calm' class bu-mkd5r (#3031) swept for, and the shared QueryBoundary primitive (loading/error/empty priority contract) exists and is adopted in ~47 files but not here. useMemoryInspect also has no placeholderData, so kind-pill switches during an active search flash the same false verdict.

findings.title: Intent-prefetch was built once (RowLink/DisclosureRow/EntityFinder) but the app's highest-traffic doors never got it
findings.detail: prefetch-registry maps exactly 3 targets (/sessions/:id, /approvals/:id, /timeline) and usePrefetchOnIntent is wired into only RowLink, DisclosureRow, and EntityFinder. Meanwhile: (a) SessionTable — the primary sessions list — opens its drawer via plain <tr onClick>; the drawer reads exactly the registry-mapped ["session-detail-global", id] key, but no hover prefetch fires, so every drawer open is a cold fetch behind a skeleton (only pinned failed rows are pre-warmed via useSessionErrorExcerpts); (b) at least 9 session/approval doors across surfaces are raw <Link>s that bypass the hook entirely (ApprovalsPage:657, SpendPage:777/1506, CalendarWorkspacePage:1623/2140, notification-feed:250, SessionDossier:330/366, qa/SessionDoors:39, EpisodeDetailPage:133, ButlerApprovalsTab:113); (c) sidebar FlatNavLinks (plain NavLink, Sidebar.tsx:203) warm nothing, and /butlers/:name — a cheap, well-known detail fetch that board cells RowLink to — is unmapped, so those RowLink prefetches no-op. The mechanism exists; adoption is 3 components deep.
