findings.title: ["decisions"] (Decision Desk) has no update path — not in the event-cache manifest and no refetchInterval; the manifest's own opt-in design let it slip through
findings.detail: useDecisions sets only queryKey+queryFn; the key appears nowhere in event-cache-manifest.ts and has no poll, so an open DecisionsPage tab updates only on window-refocus — the same infinite-staleness shape the poll-policy doc says use-notifications had before bu-01r64.3. The coverage test explicitly states new surfaces without a manifest entry are 'invisible to this test by design'. One-line note per fences: the fix belongs to the in-flight bu-01r64 update-path-manifest slice (and possibly bu-ckkpz's Decision Desk scope) — reporting only the concrete escaped key and the proof that the opt-in manifest cannot catch the next one.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-decisions.ts:13-18; frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts:38-75 (no decisions entry); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts:15-20 ('invisible to this test by design')

audits.ideal: Every surface renders last-known data instantly and forever: a filter, window, or load-more gesture never un-renders what the owner is looking at — the old data stays up, dimmed via FetchingDim, until the new answer lands (stale-while-revalidate as a lint-enforced invariant, not a per-hook courtesy). Loading, error, and empty speak through one shared primitive (QueryBoundary) so a pending state can never wear the voice of a verified verdict. Every door in the app is warm before it opens: any element that navigates or opens a drawer carries intent-prefetch keyed to the exact cache slot its destination reads, the sidebar warms each route's head query on hover, and the top five routes are pre-warmed at idle after the dashboard settles — first navigation anywhere is a cache hit. Every query key has a declared update path (bus-covered, polled, or explicitly static) verified by a sweep, not an opt-in list.
audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS never blanks what it already showed you and never guesses out loud: today a window toggle on Spend/Issues/Butler-activity wipes live panels back to skeletons, memory search answers "Nothing in the books." while it is still looking (a pending state impersonating a verdict — the doctrine's fabricated-calm failure in miniature), and instant-open is reserved for the 3 routes and 3 components that got the prefetch mechanism while every other door — including the main sessions table's own drawer — opens cold.

moves.title: Promote the never-blank floor to a lint-enforced invariant and sweep the four escaped surfaces
moves.why: th-design/interaction-speed: 'A blank screen that could have shown yesterday's data is a defect' + doctrine 'staleness never wears current-data authority' (FetchingDim pairing keeps the honesty). The repo already proved the pattern on sessions/notifications/qa/audit/search — Issues window, Spend window, ButlerActivityTab range, memory-inspect kind, and issue-occurrences load-more are the un-swept remainder. Owner payoff: window refinement becomes a zero-cost gesture on the three pages where he actually pivots time ranges.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: add placeholderData:(prev)=>prev + FetchingDim to use-issues/use-spend (4 hooks)/use-butler-analytics (4 hooks)/useMemoryInspect; convert occurrences load-more to keep-previous. Slice 2: new ESLint rule 'never-blank-floor' beside the existing poll-policy rule — any useQuery whose key embeds a runtime-variable segment must declare placeholderData or an explicit /* cold-key-ok */ marker; seed the allowlist from the current clean set. (Distinct rule from bu-k8888's poll-interval broadening; coordinate file lists so the two rules land in one eslint.config.js block.)
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-issues.ts, use-spend.ts, use-butler-analytics.ts, use-memory.ts; frontend/src/components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx (existing); frontend/eslint.config.js POLL_POLICY_FILES pattern as the template; fenced-adjacent: bu-gwhe8 (calendar only), bu-k8888 (poll rule only)

moves.title: Route memory SearchResults through QueryBoundary
moves.why: Doctrine: failure/pending must never impersonate a verdict — 'Nothing in the books.' during fetch is fabricated calm on the memory surface. QueryBoundary already encodes the loading>error>empty priority contract with role=alert; this is pure adoption of the built-once primitive.
moves.slice_plan: One slice: destructure isLoading (and isFetching for the kind-switch dim), wrap the body in QueryBoundary with a register-shaped skeleton as loadingFallback and the existing Voice empty line as emptyFallback; keep the bu-mkd5r error path. Add a vitest case asserting the empty verdict never renders while isLoading.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/memory/SearchResults.tsx; frontend/src/components/ui/query-boundary.tsx; frontend/src/hooks/use-memory.ts (placeholderData from move 1 covers the kind-pill flash)

moves.title: Generalize intent-prefetch: target-accepting hook, PrefetchLink, sidebar/route head-query warming, idle pre-warm
moves.why: th-design/interaction-speed: 'preload what the user will probably want next; warm caches at idle; prefetch on hover/focus'. The mechanism (registry + 120ms intent debounce + bus-aware staleTime) is excellent and wired 3 components deep; generalizing it makes every door in the product open warm — the single biggest perceived-speed lever left in the app.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: extend usePrefetchOnIntent to accept a PrefetchTarget directly (not just a route string); wire SessionTable rows to prefetch ["session-detail-global", id] on hover — drawer opens become cache hits. Slice 2: PrefetchLink (Link + intent handlers) and mechanically replace the ~9 raw session/approval door Links; add /butlers/:name to the registry (board RowLinks start working for free). Slice 3: per-top-level-route head-query entries in the registry + intent handlers on Sidebar FlatNavLink/MobileFlatLink. Slice 4: requestIdleCallback warm of the 4-5 highest-traffic route heads after DashboardPage's first successful paint, each at POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS staleTime so it never fights the bus.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-prefetch-on-intent.ts, frontend/src/lib/prefetch-registry.ts (keep the null-on-unmapped contract), frontend/src/components/sessions/SessionTable.tsx, frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui/RowLink.tsx; coordinate with fenced bu-zs4at (timeline prefetch cache-key filters) — do not touch the /timeline matcher's filter handling

moves.title: Fold the ["decisions"] update-path gap into bu-01r64's manifest slice and add the static sweep the coverage test admits it lacks
moves.why: The coverage test's own header concedes new surfaces bypass the opt-in manifest 'by design' — Decisions is the first proven escape (an attention surface that only updates on window refocus). Doctrine: staleness never wears current-data authority; the five-second verification loop dies if the Decision Desk shows yesterday's pending set.
moves.slice_plan: One-line coordination, not a new epic: hand the concrete key + evidence to the in-flight bu-01r64 coverage-manifest work (and flag to bu-ckkpz owners since Decision Desk is their citizen). If bu-01r64's slice doesn't already include it, the sweep shape is: a vitest that greps hooks/ for queryKey literals and asserts each root key appears in an update-path manifest classifying it bus-covered | polled | static.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-decisions.ts, frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts, frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts; fences: bu-01r64 (mechanism owner), bu-ckkpz (surface owner) — this move is coordination + the escaped instance only

audits.page: cross:interaction-speed — whole-frontend perceived-performance sweep (frontend/src/**; hooks/query configs, prefetch/poll/optimistic mechanisms, loading-state contracts)

cross:shell-discoverability (whole frontend/src sweep: command spine, shortcut registry, g-chords, list triage, help sheet, recents, empty states). NOTE: live stack was DOWN during audit (curl 127.0.0.1:42200 connection refused) — all findings source-confirmed, none live-confirmed.
audits.jarvis_gap: The shell owns a genuinely world-class discoverability chassis (one command spine, route registry, shortcut registry with shared suspend guard, '?' sheet, list triage, recents, fuzzy) — but it is an opt-in library, not a guarantee. Adoption is ~40% of pages: telemetry ledgers and every detail page have zero keyboard/palette surface, shortcut advertisement depends on each page remembering a footer component, and the palette's browsable Actions view silently degrades to 8 arbitrary global "Run <butler>" rows after the first navigation — re-breaking the exact palette-mute defect bu-qvnce.11 fixed. The single most JARVIS-like verb (talk to your butlers) has no chord. A JARVIS shell makes every surface's verbs reachable from one keyboard surface with zero per-page opt-in; today discoverability is a convention pages can (and do) forget.
audits.ideal: Discoverability by construction, not by convention: (1) the command registry ranks scopes (page > widget > global) so the current page's verbs always lead the palette, with the ~12 global "Run <butler>" rows collapsed behind a quota; (2) the Page primitive auto-renders the on-page hint strip from useShortcutHintEntries, so any registered shortcut is advertised where it works — per-page ListTriageFooterHint opt-in deleted; (3) every row ledger goes through useListTriage and every detail page exports its hot verbs (copy id, open trace) as palette commands via one shared helper — enforced by a lint/test manifest, same pattern as the poll-policy and axe skip-manifest gates; (4) one roster-aware route source feeds sidebar, palette, g-chords, and the '?' sheet identically; (5) chat gets a first-class chord advertised on the button, in the palette, and in the help sheet.

findings.title: Palette empty-query Actions group drops page verbs after first navigation (global 'Run <butler>' scope wins the slice)
findings.evidence: command-registry.tsx:77-83 (register() Map.set appends new scope at END; navigation unregisters the old page scope and re-inserts the new page's scope after the long-lived global scope), EntityFinder.tsx:473-479 (empty query: actionMatches = allActions.slice(0, 8), no ranking), GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx:36-57 (registers one 'Run <name>' per roster butler; roster/ has 12 butlers), FloatingChatWidget.tsx:522-533 ('Talk to Butlers' also in a long-lived scope). On first load page effects fire before GlobalActionsRegistrar (tree order), masking the bug; after ANY route change the order is [12x Run <butler>, Talk to Butlers, page scope] and slice(0,8) shows only Run commands.
findings.detail: The browsable-before-typing Actions group (bu-qvnce.11's fix for 'palette-mute') regresses for every page after the first navigation: ApprovalsPage's 'Approve next', Spend's rule commands, Calendar/Chronicles verbs never appear at empty query. Fuzzy search still finds them, so the defect is invisible in typed-query tests. Failure scenario: open /, navigate to /approvals, press Cmd+K — Actions shows 8 'Run <butler>' rows; 'Approve next' (with its taught [a] binding) is absent.

findings.title: Shortcut advertisement is per-page opt-in and already uneven: Sessions has j/k/[/]/y with no on-page hint strip
findings.evidence: SessionsPage.tsx:308-360 (hand-rolled moveSelection + useRegisterShortcut for j/k/[/]/y, no ListTriageFooterHint import — grep confirms only ApprovalsPage/IssuesPage/NotificationsPage/DecisionsPage/DashboardPage render list-triage-footer.tsx); ButlerDetailPage/ChroniclesPage/CalendarWorkspacePage likewise register shortcuts visible only in the '?' sheet; use-list-triage.ts:24-31 documents the footer contract Sessions bypasses.
findings.detail: The discoverability bar says a shortcut is advertised where the action lives. Five triage pages render the footer strip; the sixth keyboard-heavy list (Sessions, the trace spine's front page) advertises nothing on-page, and detail/workspace pages advertise only via '?'. The pattern was built once (ListTriageFooterHint) but its rendering was never lifted into the Page primitive, so each new page can silently forget it — Sessions already did.

findings.title: Telemetry ledgers and all detail pages have zero keyboard/palette surface — the chassis's adoption boundary is exactly the pages the trace spine lands on
findings.evidence: grep for useRegisterShortcut/useRegisterCommands/useListTriage returns nothing in TimelinePage.tsx, AuditLogPage.tsx, IngestionTimelinePage.tsx, MemoryPage.tsx (page level), SystemPage.tsx, ButlersPage.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx, QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx, EntityDetailPage.tsx, ConnectorDetailPage.tsx. SessionDetailPage.tsx:23-61: the dossier deep-linked from 10+ surfaces (its own header comment) exposes no 'Copy session id' / 'Open trace timeline' command or shortcut — SessionsPage has y-to-copy (SessionsPage.tsx:344-356) but the detail page you actually land on from a notification does not; trace nav exists only as an inline link (SessionDossier.tsx:321-335).
findings.detail: Signal → session → evidence is the doctrine's hot path, and its terminal doors are mouse-only. Timeline/Audit/Ingestion ledgers are row lists with no j/k despite useListTriage existing precisely for them (its own doc comment names 'Dashboard's Needs-attention list, Issues, Notifications' as the generalization targets — the telemetry ledgers were never picked up).

findings.title: 'Talk to Butlers' — the JARVIS front door — has no chord anywhere
findings.evidence: FloatingChatWidget.tsx:522-533 (PaletteCommand with no binding field, perform: setOpen(true)); use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:14-72 (no chat chord among global bindings); shortcut-hints.tsx STATIC_SHORTCUTS lists only Ctrl+K, /, ?.
findings.detail: A keyboard route exists (Cmd+K → 'talk' → Enter) so this passes the floor, but the highest-frequency conversational action has no accelerator while lower-frequency page verbs (approve, probe-all) have single-key bindings. The discoverability bar: chords for hot actions; the widget button's tooltip and palette row advertise nothing.

findings.title: g-chords and the '?' help sheet are not roster-gated, while the palette's Pages group is — same policy, three of four entry points unfixed
findings.evidence: route-registry.ts:82-87 (G_CHORD_ROUTES built statically from ALL_ROUTES, no butler filter); shortcut-hints.tsx:33-42 (useChordShortcuts maps ALL_ROUTES unfiltered); EntityFinder.tsx:366-375 (availablePages filters by installedButlers — bu-r4msa #3301 gated only this consumer); use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:62-66 navigates blindly.
findings.detail: g+h navigates to /health and the help sheet teaches 'Go to Health' even when the health butler is absent from the roster — the exact drift class bu-r4msa fixed for the palette, reintroduced by consuming the registry pre-filter. The registry is the right single source; the roster filter just lives in the wrong layer (one consumer instead of the source).

findings.title: EmptyState supports a teaching action but almost no call site uses it (~2 of 20+)
findings.evidence: empty-state.tsx:42-47 (action prop exists); grep '<EmptyState' across frontend/src with -A4 finds action= passed only ~2 times across 20 non-ui consumer files.
findings.detail: The bar: an empty list shows the action that fills it. The primitive was built with the affordance; the fleet's empty states overwhelmingly render title+description only, so first-use surfaces describe absence instead of teaching the filling verb (connect account, create rule, trigger butler).

findings.title: Pending g-chord state is invisible for its 1s window
findings.evidence: use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:54-60 (window.__pendingGNav = true with a 1000ms setTimeout; no UI, no announcer call — shell-announcer.ts is available one directory over).
findings.detail: Pressing g gives zero feedback; a wrong second key silently no-ops. A tiny 'g …' chip (and an announce()) would make the chord system self-teaching mid-keystroke — the progressive-power nudge the discoverability bar asks for.

moves.title: Scope-ranked command registry: page verbs always lead the palette
moves.why: North star 'keyboard-first' + bu-qvnce.11's own acceptance ('verbs invisible until the first keystroke' must not recur) — fixes the major empty-query regression where 12 global 'Run <butler>' rows evict the current page's verbs after any navigation. Owner payoff: Cmd+K on any page always opens showing what THIS page can do.
moves.integration_points: src/lib/command-registry.tsx (add scope kind: 'page'|'global' to register(); sort in useCommandMenuActions or expose grouped), src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:472-479 (per-group quota at empty query, e.g. page verbs first then ≤3 global), GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx + FloatingChatWidget.tsx declare kind:'global'.

moves.why: Discoverability doctrine: 'a shortcut listed only in a help page doesn't exist' — Sessions already shipped j/k/[/]/y with zero on-page advertisement, proving the opt-in decays. moves.title: Keyboard parity for telemetry ledgers and detail-page verbs
moves.why: Unbroken trace spine 'every clause a door' — the doors at the END of the spine (Timeline, Audit, Ingestion ledger, SessionDetail) are mouse-only while sibling lists have full triage. Owner payoff: land on a session from a notification and press y/t to copy id / open trace without touching the mouse.

moves.title: First-class chat chord
moves.why: Vision: the owner talks to the system — the single most JARVIS-like verb should cost one keystroke, not a palette round-trip. 'Defaults for the first use, accelerators for the tenth.'
moves.integration_points: use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts or a useRegisterShortcut in FloatingChatWidget (must respect the suspend guard + not collide with page keys — a modifier chord like Ctrl+J, or g-family 'g c' is taken by Contacts so prefer Ctrl+J), FloatingChatWidget.tsx palette command gains binding:[…], button aria-label/title advertises it, shortcut-hints.tsx STATIC_SHORTCUTS row.
moves.slice_plan: One PR: chord + binding metadata + tooltip + help-sheet row + test that chord toggles and is suspended inside editable fields/modals.

moves.title: Roster-gate the whole route spine, not one consumer
moves.why: bu-r4msa's own rationale ('the registry is the single source of truth so entry points can never drift') is violated by fixing only the palette — chords and the help sheet still teach routes for absent butlers. Failure never impersonates health: don't teach a door that opens onto a missing butler.

moves.slice_plan: 1) Hook + palette/help-sheet consumers; 2) chord navigation gating + collision/coverage tests extended in route-registry.test.ts.

moves.title: Empty-states-teach sweep with a manifest gate
moves.why: Discoverability bar: 'an empty list shows the action that fills it.' The primitive has the affordance (empty-state.tsx action prop); ~18 of 20 call sites waste it. Same enforcement pattern the repo already trusts (poll-policy ESLint, axe skip-manifest): a test that lists EmptyState call sites without action and requires an explicit exemption.

findings.title: Cool hues (blue/purple/sky) are an unregistered shadow palette carrying 7+ meanings; the Dispatch ESLint palette guard bans only warm hues
findings.evidence: eslint.config.js:61 — the Tailwind-palette-class ban regex covers only (red|green|emerald|amber|yellow|orange); blue/purple/sky/violet/indigo/teal/cyan pass lint. Live instances (31 hits / 18 files, all in the served worktree): approvals info-banners with blue Card fills + blue-600 CTA buttons (components/approvals/rule-promotion-banner.tsx:32,36-37,67; autonomy-suggestions-banner.tsx:51,55-56,88; autonomy-panel.tsx:62; rule-promotion-stats.tsx:68; pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:144); ingestion replay_pending blue badge/dot (components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:74,173; HourFlameStrip.tsx:213; TimelineTab.tsx:1199); schedules 'job' kind badge bg-blue-600 (components/schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx:152); QA pr_open/drafted (components/butler-detail/ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:61,81,186; components/qa/PRPanel.tsx:29); timeline lane dots session=bg-blue-500 / notification=bg-purple-500 (components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx:54-56 — a second inline lane palette, same class of defect as the known chronicles lane-taxonomy one but a NEW instance, touched as recently as bu-hmdqz.14); relationship 'primary' marker text-blue-500 (components/relationship/ContactChannelCard.tsx:364,415). Spec violated: dashboard-design-language spec.md § Surface Palette 'No invented colors' + § State Color Discipline (exactly three state colors). Blue simultaneously means: job-kind, PR-open, replay-pending, autonomy-suggestion info, session lane, primary channel, education 'completed' — one hue, seven meanings. Meanwhile the --categorical-1..12 ramp built for exactly this (index.css:193-204, shipped #3358) has exactly ONE consumer: components/chronicles/lane-taxonomy.ts (grep -rln 'var(--categorical-' → 1 file).
findings.detail: The 07-12 lens knowns cover the .ts hex blind spot and bg-[var(--red)] dodge; this is the third and largest guard hole — Tailwind *class names* for cool hues are entirely unguarded, and the categorical ramp shipped as a token set without an adoption sweep, so every pre-existing blue surface kept its shadow palette.

findings.title: State colors on background fills — new violator instances beyond the known bg-[var(--red)] dodge ledger
findings.evidence: components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:50 — 'ingested' (the routine, healthy status) renders as a solid green filled badge: bg-[var(--green)] text-white (spec: state color on foreground/border only; green fill is never permitted — the attention-tint exception is red/amber 4-7% + rail only, and healthy states get no loudness at all). components/butler-detail/ButlerManagementTab.tsx:404-406 — bg-[var(--green)]/10 and bg-[var(--red)]/10 chip tints (green tint categorically outside the exception; red tint without the 2px rail, not an attention row). components/approvals/rule-promotion-banner.tsx:67 and autonomy-suggestions-banner.tsx:88 — bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white CTA buttons violate § Button Forms (commit button is inverted fg/bg, 'never colored'; 'The system has no rounded gradient CTA anywhere'). Both banners survived the recent approvals work (#3382 fingerprint v2, #3413 stale-promotion reconcile) untouched.
findings.detail: StatusBadge and the approvals banners sit on two of the highest-traffic attention surfaces (ingestion timeline, approvals). The 'ingested' green fill also inverts the composure doctrine: the routine state is the loudest element in the row.

findings.title: Education surfaces ship light-only Tailwind chips that break in the designed-first dark theme
findings.evidence: components/education/QuizHistoryList.tsx:13,18,19 (bg-blue-100 text-blue-800, bg-purple-100 text-purple-800, bg-sky-100 text-sky-800), CurriculumActions.tsx:18 (completed: bg-blue-100 text-blue-800), NodeDetailPanel.tsx:11 (reviewing: bg-blue-100 text-blue-800) — no dark: variants and no tokens, so in dark-primary mode (doctrine: 'dark is the designed-first mode', spec Purpose section) these render as bright pastel pills on oklch(0.145) ground. EducationPage.tsx:64,80,100,123 also carries 4x 'text-2xl font-bold' H1s against the weight-500 rule.
findings.detail: Education is the most visibly pre-Dispatch surface left: an entire generation-1 shadcn idiom (filled pastel chips, bold H1s) untouched by any of the four pursuit epics.

findings.title: Two title vocabularies and a bold-KPI idiom contradict the type system; canonical primitives exist but are unadopted, and one file cites a stale 'font-bold is the H1 standard' doctrine
findings.evidence: Spec § Type System: display/title weight 500, 'no font-bold on display text'; § KPI Strip: mega-number sans 500. Violations: components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:158 (text-2xl font-bold, error branch) vs :192 (text-2xl font-semibold, loaded branch) — two weights for the same H1 in one file; pages/EducationPage.tsx:64,80,100,123 (font-bold); components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:13 comment claims 'text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight (design-language.md H1 standard)' — a stale citation contradicting the current spec. Bold KPI mega-numbers: ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab.tsx:138,321; ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:155; ButlerEducationReviewsTab.tsx:261,611; components/education/MasterySummaryCards.tsx:61; components/notifications/notification-stats-bar.tsx:54,84,116,134; components/costs/CostWidget.tsx:54; pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2754,2775 (font-semibold H1). Meanwhile weight-500 primitives exist and are correct: components/ui/page.tsx:108 (Title as h1) and :153-163 (EditorialHeadingBlock, 44px/500/-0.025em), components/ui/Display.tsx.
findings.detail: Newer pages (SettingsConsolePage:580, QaOverviewPage:434, ApprovalsPage:1588) use font-medium — the drift is generational, and nothing stops regression: no lint selector pairs font-bold with text-2xl/3xl/4xl.

findings.title: Chat TypingIndicator uses animate-bounce — explicitly forbidden motion — and ignores the spec's purpose-built 'composing…' Process Status Pill
findings.evidence: components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx:10,14,18 — three staggered animate-bounce dots (infinite bounce loop). Spec § Motion Vocabulary: 'Forbidden: spring physics, bounce… "delight" of any kind. Calm is the feature.' audits.page: cross:visual-language (entire frontend/src sweep)
audits.jarvis_gap: JARVIS reads as one hand that never contradicts itself; this frontend still reads as three generations sharing a wardrobe. The Dispatch spine is real and enforced — hex is banned in JSX, warm Tailwind hues are banned, skeleton-pulse is dead, oklch tokens + a categorical ramp + weight-500 title primitives all exist. But every fence has one cool-hue-shaped hole: blue/purple/sky classes dodge the palette guard and carry seven unregistered meanings across approvals, ingestion, schedules, QA, timeline, and relationship; the categorical ramp shipped with exactly one consumer; 'ingested' — the calmest possible state — is the loudest element in its row (solid green fill); education still renders light-only pastel chips in a dark-first product; and the newest surface (chat) bounces three dots in a perpetual delight-loop the doctrine explicitly forbids. The gap is not missing mechanisms — it is that mechanisms ship without adoption sweeps and guards ship covering only the hues that were misused last time.
audits.ideal: One palette, fully fenced: every color class or var in frontend/src resolves to a named token with exactly one recorded meaning — three state hues (foreground/border only, attention-tint exception intact), twelve categorical hues for local taxonomies (timeline lanes, quiz kinds, PR states, replay status if it stays a category at all — though replay_pending is really StateDot 'waiting'), butler hues confined to ButlerMark. The ESLint Dispatch layer bans ALL Tailwind hue classes (not six warm ones) plus animate-spin/animate-bounce, so the guard is hue-complete and motion-complete. One title voice (weight 500 via Title/EditorialHeadingBlock, KpiStrip for mega-numbers), one pending vocabulary (static placeholder for initial load, FetchingDim for refetch, the mono 'composing…' process pill for LLM work — no spinners, no bouncing dots), one Meter primitive, one global :focus-visible rule in index.css that shadcn primitives inherit instead of overriding. Every future primitive lands with its adoption sweep and its lint fence in the same PR — a token without consumers-migrated is treated as unfinished work.

audits.page: dashboard — route / (Overview triage cockpit: briefing, Needs-attention list, KPI strip, Butler index, Now list, cost band). Audited live against http://127.0.0.1:42200 + source at /home/tze/gt/butlers (worktree HEAD ≈ origin/main@46f699036). Known-ledger rediscoveries dropped: approvals-source voicelessness, CostWidget $0.00 fabrication, sessions-24h triple count, board degraded-aggregate flags unconsumed (stripe_source_error/sessions_source_error still unread by model.ts), Now-list copy doors.
audits.jarvis_gap: Since 07-12 the cockpit has grown real honesty muscle — butlers/issues/notifications/fleet-halt source deaths now speak as role="alert" attention rows, inline approve/deny/defer carries the same 5s undo contract as /approvals, and j/k/a/d/x/u keyboard triage with an honest footer hint shipped. But the page still fails the five-second test on coherence and time-honesty. Live right now it says three different numbers about the same reality in one glance: headline "One thing needs you now." (server counts severity=="high" only), elaboration "7 items requiring attention" (server total), and a client-derived list of ~11 rows — because TWO attention models still exist (Python dashboard_briefing.py vs TS model.ts) and the client never consumes the composed verdict the briefing classified from. Its loudest persistent alarm — "87 failed notifications" — is an all-time cumulative counter (84 from July, 3 from June) with no window, no age, and no lifecycle that can ever return it to calm: staleness wearing current-data authority, and the LLM briefing inherits it as urgent narrative. The "Now" list's recent-activity rows are raw system-prompt heads ("# Memory Consolidation You are performing memory consolidation for the butler ecosystem…") with no timestamps — machine plumbing where the owner's life should be. The approval rows dump ~550-char multi-paragraph `why` texts under tool-name titles, turning the flagship list into a wall of text. And the cost band below is a frozen monument: all-time top sessions headed by a $92 QA session from May 23, in off-dialect shadcn cards. JARVIS would speak one arithmetic truth, in human words, time-stamped, and let every clause open its evidence from the keyboard.
audits.ideal: The Overview opens with one attention model computed once — server-composed, verdict-classified, returned with the briefing — so the headline count, the elaboration prose, and the Needs-attention rows are projections of the same array and can never disagree; every number on the page is a door (headline "3 things need you now" clicks to the three rows; each row deep-links to its evidence with the filter predicate baked in). Every signal carries its window and its age: "9 failed notifications · 24h" with a door to the failed view, never a cumulative ratchet; activity rows say "2m ago"; anything older than its cadence wears an explicit staleness pixel. The Now list renders the owner's life and the fleet's real work in human sentences — internal housekeeping (consolidation, heartbeats) collapses into a single quiet clause — and approval rows read as decisions ("Link 3blue1brown@… to entity 3Blue1Brown — approve?") clamped to two lines with blast-radius glyphs. The whole page is one Dispatch dialect including the cost band (windowed today/7d, degraded-voiced), and the keyboard loop is complete: j/k roves, a/d/x/u acts, Enter/o opens the selected row's evidence — signal to root cause in under five seconds without touching the mouse.

moves.title: Life-event ripple: Switchboard-brokered domain-event pub/sub (travel books a trip → finance, health, home, relationship all react unprompted)
moves.why: vision.md's core loop is trigger→classify→route, but today the only cross-butler triggers are owner messages and cron — one butler's state change never reaches the butlers whose domains it touches. This is the definitional 'what none can accomplish alone': a booked flight should ripple into a budget envelope (finance MANIFESTO), timezone/medication plan (health), away-mode arming (home), and 'friends in that city' (relationship) without the owner asking. Requires a Switchboard MANIFESTO amendment adding 'domain event brokerage' as a fourth responsibility (it already brokers messages, notify intents, and insights — this is the same staffer role). Distinct from openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md (butler-LOCAL calendar/deadline triggers) and from the known-cut commissions primitive (owner-initiated tasking; this is state-change-initiated propagation).
moves.integration_points: New spec openspec/specs/cross-butler-domain-events/; tables public.domain_events (typed event + payload + publishing session id) and switchboard.event_subscriptions (subscriber butler, event_type, seeded matrix derived from manifestos); new core tool publish_domain_event registered non-STAFFER exactly like delegation (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:55-68 pattern); dispatch via existing route() (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/route.py) to an event_receive receipt tool mirroring delegate_receive; every dispatch ledgered with event id → session request_id so the ripple is walkable on the trace spine; RFC + owner gate (new brokerage responsibility on a critical staffer).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Tables + publish tool + ledger, no subscribers (S); 2) route()-dispatched event_receive + one seeded edge travel.trip_booked→finance with an end-to-end trace test; 3) subscription matrix for health/home/relationship + dashboard door from domain_event row → fanned sessions; 4) MANIFESTO amendment + spec ratification + attention-ledger integration so ripple-triggered notifies cite their originating event.

moves.title: Thread delegation onto the trace spine and wake the asker (builds on known-cut 'close the delegation loop' — adds the session-linkage and verification layer that item didn't name)
moves.why: The north star demands every clause be a door on signal→session→evidence; delegation is the one channel whose whole point is proving butler-to-butler work, yet its ledger rows link to no session on either side and answers strand in an unread table. Serves cross-butler-delegation spec's Ledger Of Record requirement in spirit — the record exists but is unwalkable and unconsumed. Owner payoff: the first time two butlers demonstrably answer a question together, verifiable in five seconds.
moves.integration_points: Migration adding asking_session_id/answering_session_id/request_id to public.delegation_ledger (core chain — serialize the core_NNN number); delegate_receive's scheduled task stamps answering_session_id at fire time (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:304-328); new delegate_deliver receipt symmetric to delegate_receive so delegate_answer wakes the ASKING butler with the answer text via route(); one adoption clause in roster/shared/AGENTS.md ('when a question crosses your domain, delegate_ask — never guess another domain's facts'); dashboard delegation panel with doors to both sessions via existing GET /api/sessions?request_id filter (src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:420); weekly canary delegation from general as a liveness drill.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Ledger session-linkage columns + delegate_deliver wake path; 2) shared AGENTS.md adoption clause + canary drill; 3) dashboard ledger panel with two-session doors; 4) spec delta adding Answer Consumption + Traceability requirements to cross-butler-delegation.

moves.title: Briefing→insight bridge: give the broker all seven voices from highlights the fleet already computes (concretizes known-cut 'full-roster insight participation' via a new zero-LLM mechanism)
moves.why: The insight digest (RFC 0011) is the fleet's one collaborative owner-facing product, and it hears 3 of 9 voices with 96% concentration in relationship. The deterministic briefing jobs ALREADY extract priority-tagged highlights for all 7 specialists daily (live 7/7); bridging high/medium highlights into propose_insight_candidate gives the broker full-roster input in one PR — no new LLM cost, no roster prompt changes, education/home/lifestyle join without ever having had an insight job. Serves every domain manifesto's proactivity promise and vision.md's 'butlers surface timely insights without being asked'.

moves.title: Single-voice reply composition: lead butler synthesizes one answer for multi-domain owner messages
moves.why: purpose-and-single-pane doctrine on the outbound side: JARVIS answers as one mind, not as a committee replying in fragments. Today a mixed question fans to N butlers who each independently notify() the originating chat (ingress-injection spec) — the owner gets N partial replies in arbitrary order. Designate the highest-scoring classification target as lead; non-lead butlers return structured contributions (reusing the delegation ledger's ask/answer machinery, giving move #2's plumbing a second consumer); lead composes one reply with per-butler attribution; Messenger delivers once. Serves the Switchboard contract's 'fanout for multi-domain messages' responsibility — amends it from parallel-independent to lead-composed. This is composed judgment no single butler can produce.
moves.integration_points: roster/switchboard/tools/routing/contracts.py (SubrequestV1: add role lead|contributor next to fanout_mode:464); classification (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/classify.py) picks lead by score; contributor sessions answer into delegation_ledger rows keyed to the shared request_id instead of calling notify(); lead's ingress-injection prompt gains a compose-and-cite step; ingress-injection + conversation-decomposition spec deltas; messenger notify.v1 unchanged (origin_butler lineage already retained per roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Contract role field + lead selection, contributors still reply directly (no behavior change, telemetry only); 2) contributor→ledger return path + lead compose for 2-butler fanouts behind a switchboard config flag; 3) timeout/degradation clause — if a contributor misses its SLA the lead replies with an explicit 'finance's view pending' rather than silence or fabricated completeness; 4) spec ratification + e2e.

Not a rediscovery of Move #15 (producers, QC-graded): this is the missing visibility/verification layer above it. Serves RFC 0009's shared-awareness intent and docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md.

moves.title: Cross-butler burst coalescing at Messenger: lift bu-o8233's per-butler digest one level so simultaneous multi-butler sends arrive as one message
moves.why: The ripple move (#1) and today's cron alignment both create bursts where several butlers message the owner within the same minute; bu-o8233 coalesces only within ONE butler's deferred_notifications flush, and Messenger executes each cross-butler notify.v1 independently — four buzzes for one life event. A deterministic N-minute coalesce window (medium/low priority; high bypasses) composing same-channel/same-recipient intents with per-butler attribution treats owner attention as the shared resource it is. Requires a Messenger MANIFESTO amendment: its contract currently forbids initiating autonomous behavior — a deterministic flush job is transport batching, but the contract must say so explicitly (vision rule 6).

moves.slice_plan: 1) Queue + window for telegram only, 2-minute window, ledger-stamped; 2) composed-message format with per-butler sections + reply-targeting rules; 3) email/whatsapp channels + spec ratification.

audits.page: eco:collaboration
audits.jarvis_gap: Upgraded from 07-12's 'weak': two of the four dead channels now carry real traffic — the context bus has live producer rows actively gating notifications (health 'sleeping' at audit time, clean supersession on general's 'meeting'), and briefing participation recovered to 7/7 fresh daily contributions (missing_butlers=[] three days running). But the ecosystem still only passes notes; it never produces a joint outcome. Delegation remains at zero rows ever with no roster adoption and answers that strand unread; the insight chorus is still 3 of 9 voices at 96% single-butler concentration; a multi-domain question gets N uncoordinated replies instead of one composed answer; and no butler's state change ever triggers another butler — the only cross-domain triggers are the owner and the clock. JARVIS coordinates domains as one organism around life events and speaks with one voice; Butlers has working channels and zero joint work products, and what little collaboration exists (delegation, context suppression) is unwalkable on the trace spine and invisible to the owner.
audits.ideal: One life event entering any butler ripples deterministically to every domain it touches, the affected butlers' contributions compose into a single attributed voice on one owner channel, and every hop — event, dispatch, session, reply, suppression — is a door on the trace spine verifiable in five seconds; the delegation, context, insight, and briefing channels all carry daily traffic from all nine domains, and the owner can see at a glance both what the fleet jointly concluded and why it chose silence.

audits.page: eco:connectors
audits.jarvis_gap: Since 07-12 the fleet has genuinely hardened the existing roster (auth-revocation vs API-degradation classification #3360, Telegram user health #3351, WhatsApp bridge wait+bounded backfill #3367/#3392, HA allowlist defaults #3375, owner-event backfill #3390) and the bu-dyq22 roadmap lane holds the six known next-connectors — reliability doctrine (RFC 0018: harden before broaden) is being honored. But re-grading against the pursuit question, the lens stays functional, not solid: the manifesto-promise-vs-substrate audit method the 07-12 run introduced still finds unclaimed gaps one ring further out. Travel's document-expiry promise is backed by a literally never-written table whose only tool is trip-scoped attach; home's interactive energy Q&A is misdirected by a skill citing tools that don't exist (while the data sits live in the HA snapshot); the outdoor-conditions half of the morning environment briefing is dropped despite weather.forecast_home already being ingested with zero readers; and the relationship butler's 'who you've talked to and when' feed is structurally deaf to voice calls — the channel most correlated with the inner Dunbar layers its own manifesto says get priority. The pattern across all four: perception debt now lives less in 'missing external services' than in promised clauses with no feed, plus a small set of genuinely new external surfaces (national environment feeds, telephony metadata, transit disruption, breach events) that no prior run has proposed and that all fit the existing doctrine profile (keyless/local-first or explicitly paid-gated).
audits.ideal: Every binding manifesto clause has a named feed or a formal amendment — audited each pursuit run, with 'promise without substrate' treated as a doctrine defect (vision.md rule 6). Concretely for this ring: standing owner documents (passport, visas, insurance) live in a person-scoped registry with expiry radar fed by onboarding capture plus Gmail renewal-notice triage; the home butler answers energy questions through real tools over the HA statistics it already ingests, and its morning briefing pairs indoor sensors with the outdoor forecast and national environment feeds (haze PSI, UV, dengue proximity) that a Singapore owner actually acts on; the relationship butler's interaction ledger includes call metadata (never content) via the proven OwnTracks-style webhook pattern so 'quiet for a while' is true across channels; commute-window transit disruptions feed the context bus's existing 'commuting' signal so the switchboard can time and suppress delivery intelligently; and credential compromise is perceived from the outside (breach-event feed) not just managed from the inside. All new capture stays doctrine-clean: HA-subsumption checked first, keyless/free preferred, paid keys surfaced as explicit owner decisions per RFC 0018, metadata-only for high-sensitivity channels, and every shipped connector carries a normative connector-* spec.

audits.page: eco:inference — trigger→spawn→act loop (model_routing.py, spawner.py, memory consolidation dispatch, live catalog/ledger)
audits.jarvis_gap: The 07-12 landings (failover vocabulary, derived breaker, hourly verify) closed the honesty gap in model selection — resolution is now genuinely closed-loop (breaker CTE inlined in every resolver, model_routing.py:322-378). But the loop itself still hemorrhages money and latency: a self-sustaining memory-consolidation feedback loop is burning ~34M uncached tokens/week spawning ~586 no-op LLM sessions/day on one butler alone (each session's own output is re-stored as an episode and re-consolidated 10 minutes later, forever); owner-facing message→reply is ~60s p50 / ~134s p95 (classification 19.9s + route 39.2s) with zero session reuse, zero streaming, and cold CLI boot per dispatch; every spawn pays 8+ sequential DB round trips to a Tailscale-remote Postgres including a full month-to-date ledger pricing pass; and the one latency decomposition the system does measure (codex spawn_latency_ms) is computed then dropped on the floor. JARVIS answers in seconds and never bills you for talking to itself; this system talks to itself ~5M tokens/day and makes the owner wait a minute.
audits.ideal: Every dispatch is a priced, prioritized, single-round-trip decision: one SQL gate returns (candidate, quota, ceiling, permission, rule) in one RTT against a locally-maintained MTD counter; owner-interactive dispatches ride a dedicated lane with pre-warmed runtime workers (MCP handshake and static system prompt already resident) so message→reply is bounded in single-digit seconds; maintenance work (consolidation, backfill, QA) runs on a separate starved lane through the api-direct adapter — cheap non-Claude models, text-in/JSON-out, no CLI boot, no MCP config — and is dead-banded so it never runs when there is nothing real to consolidate; the memory loop treats butler self-narration (consolidation/maintenance outputs) as exhaust, never as experience, so the flywheel can only be driven by the owner's life, not by itself; and every session row carries a phase-decomposed latency spine (gate_ms, boot_ms, model_ms) so 'where did the 39 seconds go' is a door, not a research project.

findings.title: Consolidation ouroboros: consolidation sessions' own outputs are stored as episodes and re-consolidated forever — ~586 no-op LLM sessions/day on travel alone
findings.evidence: spawner.py:2016-2022 stores an episode for EVERY successful memory-enabled session with no trigger_source carve-out; openspec/specs/core-spawner/spec.md:234 mandates this unconditionally; memory/__init__.py:52-86 registers memory_consolidation_backfill at */10 min per butler; consolidation.py:244-247 spawns via cc_spawner.trigger(trigger_source='schedule:consolidation') whose success re-enters the episode store. LIVE: travel.sessions last 24h = 586 schedule:consolidation sessions (avg 21.6s, avg 16.6K uncached input each); 612 of 637 travel.episodes rows written in last 24h are consolidation JSON outputs ('new_facts': [] ...); token_usage_ledger 7d purpose=schedule:consolidation = 1,783 calls, 33.9M uncached + 19.1M cached input tokens, 36% cache hit, travel = 1,755 of them averaging 129 output tokens (i.e. empty results). Loop introduced when #3285 (a12894e34) routed scheduled consolidation through Spawner; no bead exists (bd list --title-contains consolidation: only bu-6t8ix, unrelated).
findings.detail: Self-sustaining: each run claims the previous run's output-episode (pending=1 observed between beats), spawns a ~27K-token workhorse-tier session, whose output becomes the next pending episode. Also occupies ~3.5 slot-hours/day of the process-global 3-slot spawn cap (spawner.py:138) and burns Codex/workhorse quota that interactive lanes need. Fix requires a spec delta: core-spawner spec §'store the session output as an episode' must exclude maintenance trigger sources.

findings.title: Owner-facing inference latency ~60s p50 / ~134s p95 message→reply; cold CLI boot per dispatch, no session reuse, no streaming
findings.evidence: LIVE: switchboard.sessions 7d classification p50=19,875ms p95=46,842ms (343 sessions); route sessions across general/health/finance/messenger 7d p50=39,203ms p95=87,054ms (195 sessions). Source: spawner._run creates a fresh adapter worker per attempt (spawner.py:1323-1325, create_worker()), codex.py subprocess-per-session with MCP discovery retry; result is returned only on completion (SpawnerResult, spawner.py:1896-1905) — no first-token/streaming path anywhere in the loop.
findings.detail: Classification-side SLA is a known (api-lane owner decision, not re-filed); the route-side 39.2s p50 with full cold-boot per dispatch is the un-filed half of the owner's wait.

findings.title: Pre-spawn gate chain is 8+ sequential round trips to a remote DB, including an O(month-ledger) pricing pass on EVERY dispatch
findings.evidence: spawner.py:930-1318 sequence: resolve_model_with_effective_tier (1 RTT), apply_spend_routing_rules (spend_rules fetch + optional resolve-by-model + breaker probe, model_routing.py:1143-1263), check_permission (1), check_token_quota (limits-exists + CTE, model_routing.py:1318-1324), check_monthly_ceiling → price_mtd_from_ledger which aggregates ALL current-month token_usage_ledger rows and prices them in Python on every single spawn (model_routing.py:1439-1447, 1390-1407; 3,549 MTD rows live), then provider_config, prompt override, context preamble, timezone, memory context fetches (spawner.py:1318, 1400-1432) — all sequential awaits. DB is remote over Tailscale (POSTGRES_HOST=butlers-db-dev.parrot-hen.ts.net, .env.dev).
findings.detail: Each gate is individually fail-open but collectively they add seconds of serial network latency and ~10 independent partial-failure surfaces before any model is even invoked.

findings.title: Spawn latency decomposition is measured then discarded — no evidence spine for where the 39s goes
findings.evidence: codex.py:1676-1683 computes spawn_latency_ms and mcp_server_count into last_process_info; spawner.py:1960-1972 persists only pid/exit_code/command/stderr/runtime_type/retry fields via session_process_log_write — spawn_latency_ms is never written to any table; sessions.duration_ms (t0 at spawner.py:1354) starts AFTER all pre-spawn gates, so gate time is invisible everywhere.

findings.title: Cross-schema episode misrouting still visible live: other butlers' episodes landing in travel.episodes after #3393/#3404
findings.evidence: LIVE: travel.episodes rows created in last 24h grouped by butler: travel 587, switchboard 23, general 9, lifestyle 7, relationship 3, education 3, chronicler 2, finance 2, health 1 — while switchboard.episodes also received 19 rows in the same window. Fixes ca78b32a9 (#3404) and 15788ed67 (#3393) are in the deployed worktree (origin/main@46f699036).

moves.why: Doctrine: 'earned calm — nothing fabricated' and vision's 'memory consolidation' exists to distill the OWNER's life, not butler self-narration; travel MANIFESTO promises organized travel clarity, not 250 self-referential sessions/day. Today one global Semaphore(3) (spawner.py:138,684) treats route/classification and schedule:consolidation/qa/healing identically. moves.title: Warm-worker session continuity for interactive lanes (RFC)
moves.why: Vision's conversational input channel at 60s p50 is not a butler, it is voicemail. A pre-warmed runtime worker per interactive butler (process started, MCP handshake done, static system prompt resident — composition is already cache-ordered stable-prefix-first, spawner_context.py:117-128) plus short-window conversation reuse for follow-up messages targets <15s p50 and gives multi-turn continuity the ephemeral-spawn model structurally lacks. This is the lens's biggest capability gap; no manifesto change needed — it fulfils existing promises (switchboard SLA, messenger immediacy).

findings.title: Consolidation provenance is batch-blurred: every fact/rule links to all 500 episodes in its batch
findings.detail: The consolidation executor loops over the entire batch's source_episode_ids for every emitted artifact, so provenance says 'derived from everything in the batch', not 'derived from the episodes that support this fact'. Live: switchboard has 63 facts carrying 28,669 derived_from links and 22 rules carrying 10,930 links; median AND max links-per-artifact are both 500, spanning 4,795 of 4,798 episodes (~the whole corpus). The parser's output dataclasses (NewFact/UpdatedFact/NewRule) have no per-artifact episode-citation field, and the consolidate SKILL.md never asks the LLM to cite supporting episodes, so precision is impossible today. The spec itself encodes the blur ('a derived_from link MUST be created from the new fact to each source episode'). The 'why do you believe this' trace spine (fact -> evidence) is a door onto a warehouse.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation_executor.py:153-154,198-199,222-223 (for episode_id in source_episode_ids: create_link); consolidation_parser.py:26-53 (no source-episode field); openspec/specs/module-memory/spec.md:166; live SQL: SELECT source_type, max(cnt), percentile_disc(0.5) -> fact 500/500, rule 500/500; 28,669 fact links over 4,795 distinct episode targets

findings.title: Switchboard memory hygiene jobs dead since 2026-04-07; 93.5% of episodes retained past their TTL, violating retention policy on the most sensitive schema
findings.detail: switchboard.scheduled_tasks rows memory_episode_cleanup and memory_consolidation are enabled=false, source='db', last_run 2026-04-07. Root mechanism: sync_schedules' orphaned-TOML pass disabled them, and ensure_module_default_schedule's reclaim explicitly leaves 'enabled ... left untouched' — it flips source toml->db but never re-enables, so a module-default job disabled once stays dead forever with no surface saying so. Consequence: 4,487 of 4,798 switchboard episodes (routed owner-message content, sensitivity-classed) sit past expires_at indefinitely, directly violating the memory-retention-policy TTL scenarios. Consolidation is partly mitigated by the enabled memory_consolidation_backfill variant; cleanup has no variant. All other schemas' jobs are enabled=t and current. Adjacent to filed bu-c6wjr (health surface) but this is a distinct self-heal defect + live retention breach, not a visibility gap.
findings.evidence: live SQL: switchboard.scheduled_tasks memory_episode_cleanup/memory_consolidation enabled=f, source='db', updated_at/last_run_at=2026-04-07; SELECT count(*) FROM switchboard.episodes WHERE expires_at<now() -> 4,487 of 4,798; src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:897-909 ('cron, job_args, enabled, and next_run_at are left untouched'); openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md:32-36

findings.title: Rule-maturity ladder now mints at scale but promotion is structurally unreachable: 89 candidate rules, zero application signal, and the spec-mandated rule_applications table was dropped
findings.detail: Since 07-12 the fleet went from 2 candidate rules to 89 (travel 57, switchboard 32) — consolidation is minting procedural memory at volume. But every rule has applied_count=0, success_count=0, harmful_count=0; memory_context serves candidates as guidance without recording an application; and the rule_applications table (which memory-retention-policy spec.md:53 still MANDATES with a full column contract) was dropped as write-orphaned in PR #2805 — spec-code drift in both directions. candidate->established->proven can never fire; the 07-12 'ladder has no structural consumer' finding has worsened into 'ladder has 44x the rules and zero possible input'. Note the distinct positive movement: fact confirmations went 21 -> 191 (consolidation's confirmation loop works for facts), making the rules gap the clear outlier.
findings.evidence: live SQL: travel.rules and switchboard.rules GROUP BY applied_count,success_count,harmful_count -> single row 0/0/0 (57 and 32); SELECT table_schema FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name='rule_applications' -> 0 rows; openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md:53; git 990b0d5c4 (PR #2805 drop); 191/4,437 facts with last_confirmed_at > created_at vs 21/4,017 at 07-12

findings.title: Fact->episode evidence doors dangle by design: episode cleanup deletes episodes without touching memory_links
findings.detail: run_episode_cleanup issues DELETE FROM episodes only; memory_links has no FK/cascade, so every consolidation provenance link eventually points at a deleted row once the episode's TTL passes. Live: 44 dangling episode-target links already (lifestyle 42, travel 2); switchboard shows 0 only because its cleanup job has been dead since April (finding above). Since episodes are TTL'd and facts are durable, 100% of fact->episode provenance is destined to 404 — the trace spine's evidence terminus is temporary by construction while the claim built on it is permanent.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation.py:504 (DELETE FROM episodes WHERE expires_at < now(), no link cleanup); live SQL dangling-link probe: lifestyle 42, travel 2, others 0; memory_links shape has no FK (6 columns, target_id bare)

findings.title: Fleet Knowledge failure impersonates 'no relevant knowledge', and explicit cross-butler reads are near zero
findings.detail: The catalog's one live consumer is the spawn-time Fleet Knowledge section (include_fleet_knowledge=True in the spawner hook — real cross-butler reads now happen on every session, a genuine improvement since 07-12). But _fetch_fleet_knowledge swallows every exception at logger.debug and returns [], and empty sections are omitted from context — so a dead embedding engine, absent table, or pool failure renders identically to 'the fleet knows nothing relevant', with no counter anywhere recording served-vs-failed. Meanwhile the explicit tool path is idle: 5 memory_catalog_search calls in 30 days across the 5 busiest schemas (vs 266 recalls, 389 stores), and no roster CLAUDE.md mentions the catalog. The 4,822-row catalog is maintained every 5 minutes for a consumer whose health and hit-rate are unmeasurable.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:128-130 (except Exception -> logger.debug -> return []); src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:380 (include_fleet_knowledge=True at spawn); live SQL sessions tool_calls scan 30d: cat_search relationship 0, general 2, finance 0, switchboard 3, health 0; grep roster/*/CLAUDE.md 'catalog' -> 0 hits

audits.page: eco:knowledge-graph (ecosystem lens — memory module, public.memory_catalog, public.entities, consolidation/decay/promotion lifecycle)
audits.jarvis_gap: Re-graded weak -> functional: since 07-12 the graph demonstrably grows and is read across butlers — facts 4,017 -> 4,437, fact confirmations 21 -> 191 (consolidation's reinforcement loop is real), rules minted 2 -> 89, rule_promotion_suggestions 0 -> 4 (3 confirmed), catalog 94% entity-anchored and injected into every spawned session via the Fleet Knowledge section, decision-memory writeback merged (#3400, fenced). What keeps it from solid is that the trust layer under that growth is still hollow: provenance is batch-blur (median=max 500 evidence links per artifact — a door onto a warehouse), the evidence terminus (TTL'd episodes) is temporary while the claims built on it are permanent, retention promises are silently unenforced on the most sensitive schema (93.5% of switchboard episodes past TTL for 3 months because a reclaimed schedule row stays enabled=false forever), and procedural memory can never promote (zero application signal, spec-mandated rule_applications table dropped). A JARVIS answers 'why do you believe this?' with one precise citation, keeps only what it promised to keep, and earns the right to act from rules that have provably worked — all three mechanisms exist here as scaffolding but none closes its loop.

moves.title: Cited provenance: consolidation output must name the episodes each fact/rule is derived from
moves.why: North-star 'every clause a door on an unbroken trace spine (signal -> session -> evidence)': today the fact->evidence door opens onto all 500 episodes of the batch, which is no provenance at all. Serves every memory-bearing butler's manifesto (relationship 'a complete picture', travel 'organized certainty') because trust in a remembered fact is only as good as its citation. Requires a spec delta: module-memory/spec.md:166 currently mandates the blur ('each source episode') and must become 'each cited source episode'.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation_parser.py (add source_episodes: list[int] to NewFact/UpdatedFact/NewRule; validation: non-empty, subset of batch indices, reject/dead-letter on missing citation), skills/consolidate/SKILL.md (episodes are already numbered — instruct citation), consolidation_executor.py:153/198/222 (link only cited episodes), openspec/specs/module-memory delta, tests in tests/ for parser+executor citation paths
moves.slice_plan: 1) Parser schema + SKILL.md citation instruction + strict validation (rejects fall to existing failed/dead_letter states); 2) Executor links only cited episodes + spec delta; 3) memory_events audit line records citation count so the dashboard fact detail can show 'derived from N episodes' honestly (no backfill of historical blur — old links stay, flagged batch-level in metadata)

moves.title: Evidence that outlives the episode: durable digest on the provenance link + session door
moves.why: Doctrine: 'staleness never wears current-data authority' and the trace spine must be unbroken — but episodes are TTL'd while facts are durable, so every evidence door is scheduled to 404 (44 already dangling). Snapshotting a small evidence digest (episode excerpt, session_id, occurred_at) at link time makes the citation permanent and redirects the door to the session log, which IS the spine. Serves all memory butlers; unblocks aggressive episode cleanup (see retention move) without destroying provenance.
moves.integration_points: consolidation_executor.py create_link call sites (pass digest), memory_links schema via mem_ Alembic branch migration (metadata JSONB or dedicated evidence columns: excerpt, session_id, occurred_at), src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py fact-detail provenance payload, frontend FactDetailPage provenance panel (door to /sessions/{id}), module-memory spec delta; coordinate with cited-provenance move (digest only for cited episodes keeps rows small)
moves.slice_plan: 1) Migration + executor writes digest on new links; 2) API fact-detail returns evidence digests with liveness flag (episode still present vs digest-only); 3) Frontend provenance panel: cited excerpt + session door, never a dead episode link; 4) episode cleanup freed to delete without breaking the spine (assert no-dangling-door invariant in integration tests)

moves.title: Self-healing module-default schedules + expired-retention deadman
moves.why: Failure is impersonating health: switchboard's cleanup job has been silently dead for 3 months because ensure_module_default_schedule reclaim leaves enabled=false forever, and 4,487 routed-message episodes now sit past their promised TTL — a live memory-retention-policy violation the owner cannot see. The fix is the module healing its own defaults, not just surfacing (complements filed bu-c6wjr which owns the health surface; this is the self-heal lever). Serves the switchboard infrastructure contract (durable buffer, retention) and vision.md 'runs for weeks without intervention'.

audits.ideal: The knowledge graph a JARVIS deserves: every durable belief carries a precise, permanent citation — 'derived from these 3 episodes, in this session, on this date' — that survives all retention cleanup because the evidence digest is snapshotted at consolidation time and the door lands on the session spine, never a TTL'd row. Retention is a kept promise: module-default hygiene jobs heal their own enabled-state, and a deadman clause fires the moment any schema holds expired memories. Knowledge compounds on three closed loops: facts reinforce via consolidation confirmations (already working — 21 -> 191), rules promote via recorded applications and session outcomes so 'proven' means proven, and the promoted-rule ladder eventually feeds the fenced earned-autonomy bridge. Cross-butler knowledge flows both implicitly (Fleet Knowledge in every spawn, with failure visibly distinct from absence) and on demand (entity-pivot fleet dossier: one owner question — 'what do we know about Mom?' — answered from ten schemas with per-butler provenance, freshness pixels, and sensitivity ceilings intact). Growth stays scalable because provenance, decay, and promotion are all deterministic daemon work; the LLM only ever supplies the citations and the judgments.

findings.title: Quiet-hours gate destroys notifications instead of parking them — the owner's morning corpus is deleted daily with no content persisted
findings.detail: notify()'s approvals-policy quiet-hours gate records outcome=suppressed and returns; unlike the adjacent delivery-preferences gate (which calls insert_deferred_notification with a deliver_at), it writes NO retry envelope and does not persist the message body (record_attention_event is called without metadata, and sampled ledger rows have metadata NULL). 212 suppressed/14d live, including daily medium-priority sends from home (04:05, 08:05 local), chronicler (01:20), relationship (08:00), finance (08:00), health (08:11). These are composed LLM outputs that vanish permanently — silence that is neither chosen nor reversible. bu-24lu6.3's push-on-park covers only decision approvals; the general egress path has no park.

findings.title: Insight channel dark since ~07-13: the just-landed sleeping producer suppresses the only daily routine delivery slot, so candidates expire while the owner engages at 85%

findings.title: Three divergent quiet-window implementations; the core one is end-INCLUSIVE, so 'quiet until 8' destroys the entire 08:00-08:59 morning-report band
findings.detail: core is_in_policy_quiet_hours treats quiet_end=8 as quiet through hour 8 (docstring: '08-12: hour 8..12 are quiet'); the insight broker's _is_quiet_hours is end-EXCLUSIVE (current_hour < quiet_end); the sleep producer builds a third derived window (end at quiet_end+1). Result: owner-configured 23→8 actually suppresses until 09:00 for notify() and until 09:00 via sleeping for the broker. Live daily casualties in the 8am hour: relationship 08:00:57, finance 08:00:31, home 08:05, health 08:11-08:25 — all suppressed-and-destroyed (see finding 1).

With verbosity=minimal the ceiling is 1/day against ~50-100 candidates/week, so even a perfectly-engaged owner (17/20 engaged) has >90% of insight supply expire unseen. The vision mandates automatic reduction on disengagement — it is silent on the upward direction, and the current design wastes the LLM spend that produced 1,072 expired candidates.

audits.ideal: The system's proactive voice follows the owner's actual day, not a static clock. Suppression is always a park, never a delete: anything gated by quiet hours or context signals is enveloped with its full content and a wake-anchored deliver_at, and the attention ledger's 'suppressed' outcome is reserved for genuinely chosen, content-preserved holds the owner can review. The morning is the flagship moment: butlers prepare content pre-dawn, and the instant the owner demonstrably wakes (first Telegram message, first keyboard heartbeat, home motion — not a policy mirror), the parked briefing, insights, and overnight holds flush as one coherent morning delivery. One shared quiet-window predicate with unambiguous end-exclusive semantics feeds every gate, every schedule is authored and displayed in the owner's timezone, and the scheduler refuses to silently run a notify-bearing job whose output will always be suppressed. The insight lane's budget breathes in both directions — earned up by demonstrated engagement (owner-approved, one tap), ratcheted down by disengagement — so the system speaks exactly as much as it has earned the right to.
audits.jarvis_gap: The delivery spine is now honest and the transport works (49 delivered, 'failed' outcome live, approval-parking firing), but the routine proactive lane is choked at exactly the hours the owner's day begins: everything scheduled 23:00-09:00 owner-local is destroyed rather than parked (212 messages/14d, content unrecoverable), the insight channel has delivered zero for a week because the just-landed sleeping mirror suppresses its only daily slot, and the flagship briefing fires 8 hours off its authored intent under a mislabel. JARVIS speaks when you wake; this system burns its morning material and talks at 15:15. Mechanics improved since 07-12; the owner-experienced routine channel regressed — held at functional only because afternoon sends, urgent bypass, and the ledger's honesty are real.

Serves every domain manifesto whose morning output is currently deleted (home, relationship, finance, health, chronicler). Builds on (and obsoletes) the 07-12 cut 'what I held back' recap: parked content needs no recap because it arrives. Coordinate the envelope shape with in-flight bu-24lu6.3 (decision push-on-park) rather than duplicating it — this move covers the general egress paths that epic fences off.

Drop sleeping confidence to <1.0 when policy-derived.

The lint closes the class: a notify-bearing schedule whose fire time lands inside the effective suppression window is a job whose entire owner-facing output is destroyed — the scheduler should say so at sync time, not let it run silently forever (home's 04:00 device-health-check has never reached the owner). Serves general's manifesto (the day-frame butler) and every roster author.

Keep the owner sovereign: the system never self-raises; it surfaces a deterministic suggestion ('you engaged with 17 of 20 — allow 3/day?') through the existing notify high-visibility path with a deep link to the insight settings surface (do NOT expand fenced epics bu-24lu6/bu-ckkpz — a plain notify + settings PATCH suffices). Serves switchboard's broker contract; implies a one-line vision amendment acknowledging the upward direction.

audits.page: eco:proactivity — scheduler → notify/insight egress → attention ledger → owner morning experience (ecosystem lens, live stack + source)
entities family — /entities (Plex), /entities/index, /entities/:entityId (Editorial+Workbench), /entities/concentration, /entities/circles
audits.jarvis_gap: The bones are now genuinely strong: honest degraded-source notes throughout the detail page (bu-hckjv pattern everywhere), view-local keyboard maps on Plex/Index/Detail, on-demand provenance reveals with a no-invented-provenance guarantee, a real merge-review pipeline, and the circles 422 fix visibly landed (GET /relationship/groups?limit=200 → 200 JSON; QC note only). But the surface still reads calmer and smaller than the real graph: the Plex landing silently hides 90% of the owner's people (156 of 174 are tier-1500, not drawn, not findable by the canvas's own find-as-you-type, and the "156 familiar faces" caption is not a door); the Concentration default view's headline KPIs measure the ego node itself (owner row = 50.9% share of 'knows', top-3 share 54.4% is mostly "you"), defeating the page's purpose on its landing state; archive is a one-click, no-confirm, no-undo one-way door with no archived view and no unarchive endpoint anywhere; and the staleness vocabulary the spec mandates is dormant on Concentration because last_seen is null on every live row, so unknown-age rows wear the same authority as fresh ones. Keyboard-first is 3-of-5: Concentration and Circles have no view map, and the Index cursor can walk off-screen. Against the north star (every clause a door, staleness never wears current authority, five-second verification), the gaps are all about doors and honesty-of-scale, not skins-over-stubs — this surface is real, it just under-tells the truth about how big and how old its data is.

findings.title: Archive is a one-way door: single-click, no confirm, no undo, no archived browse, no unarchive endpoint
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:220-249 ArchiveEntityButton fires the mutation directly on click (bulk archive at 329-374 DOES confirm; single does not); frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2587-2596 handleArchiveEntity archives then navigates away; roster/relationship/api/router.py:5180 POST /entities/{id}/archive sets metadata.archived='true' and every default list/queue excludes it (router.py:917, 1183-1184, 3300, 3605); grep 'unarchive' across frontend/src + roster/relationship → only the ingestion-connector variant exists; STATE_CHIPS (EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:118-122) offer unidentified/duplicate-candidate/stale but no 'archived' filter, and the relationship list endpoint has no archived param.
findings.detail: Violates the design-bar recovery criterion (undo for reversible actions, confirm for irreversible — archive gets neither) and the th-projects lifecycle-closure mandate: an archived entity exits every surface with no product path to see or reverse the decision, even though the data model (soft metadata flag) makes unarchive trivial. Fix: unarchive endpoint + 'Archived' state chip + toast-with-Undo on single archive.
