findings.evidence: Live: all concentration items return last_seen: None (src interaction_sync). ConcentrationPage.tsx:261-276 — the staleness dim (opacity-40 recede, spec'd 'a row whose most-recent observation is stale visibly recedes') only renders when entry.last_seen != null; with null the row shows no age token at all and is visually identical to a fresh row.
findings.detail: Two-part fix: (a) backend — carry last_observed_at through for interaction_sync-written edges so the field is populated; (b) frontend — render an explicit 'age unknown' token (dim dash) rather than nothing when last_seen is null, per the doctrine that staleness (including unknownness) never wears current-data authority. The invariant conf=1.0/verified=false marks on these same rows are the already-catalogued taxonomy shape-9 example — not re-filed.

findings.title: Detail-page type selector omits product/group — vocabulary drift from the index create dialog
findings.evidence: EntityDetailPage.tsx:2806 — Select items are ["person","organization","place","other"]; EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:97-104 — ENTITY_TYPES adds product and group, and CreateEntityDialog (1080-1096) lets the owner create them. A product/group entity opened in detail renders a Select whose value matches no item (empty pill) and cannot round-trip its own type.
findings.detail: Latent today (live counts: product=0, group=0 entities) but a created product entity immediately hits it. One shared ENTITY_TYPES constant should feed both.

findings.title: Index keyboard cursor can walk off-screen — no scroll-into-view on ArrowUp/Down
findings.evidence: EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1334-1345 — the keyboard map only sets cursor state; the cursored <tr> (679-693) has no ref/scrollIntoView, so on a 50-row page (PAGE_SIZE=50, EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:90) ArrowDown past the viewport moves the 2px-border cursor out of sight while focus stays on the container.

findings.title: Keyboard maps stop at 3 of 5 tabs: Concentration and Circles have no view-local map
findings.evidence: ConcentrationPage.tsx and CirclesPage.tsx contain no onKeyDown container/keyboard map (contrast PlexPage.tsx:1890-1931, EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1305-1363, EntityDetailPage.tsx:2423-2451); rows are tab-reachable buttons only — no j/k row cursor, no '/' to focus search, no Enter-from-row conventions matching the sibling tabs.
findings.detail: Same-family tabs teaching different muscle memory is a dialect inconsistency (design-bar bias 5/7). Small cost: reuse the Index cursor pattern.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade entities surface is the life graph as one navigable instrument: a Plex landing where every person and thing in the graph — all 174, not the inner 18 — is reachable in three keystrokes (type a name, Enter, record open), where rings state capacity honestly, the periphery is a door rather than a caption, and every mark's hover dossier carries tier, age, and a trace to its latest evidence; an Index that is the curation workbench (bulk keyboard ops, cursor always visible, archived entities browsable and restorable with one Undo); a Concentration balance sheet that excludes the ego node so its top-3 share actually measures who holds your world, with every row wearing its true age (including an explicit unknown-age token) and linking to the facts behind the weight; Circles fed by real butler-maintained groups with member deep-links; and a Detail dossier that keeps today's honest degraded-notes and provenance reveals while making every curation action reversible or confirmed, every fact one hop from its authoring session, and its vocabulary (types, tiers, predicates) identical to every sibling surface.

moves.title: Open the periphery: make tier-1500 people reachable from the Plex
moves.why: vision.md single-pane doctrine + north star 'every clause a door on an unbroken trace spine'; th-design discoverability bias 7 (features findable in the product itself). Today 156/174 people (live) are invisible and unfindable on the graph landing page — the owner's five-second question 'where is X?' dead-ends with '0 matches'. Payoff: the landing surface finally tells the truth about graph scale and answers name-lookup without leaving the canvas.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Extend PlexPage searchSpace with all ranking entries (tier 1500 included); Enter on a match with no drawn mark navigates to /entities/{id}. 2) Make the periphery caption a Link. 3) Add a tier filter param to GET /relationship/entities + an Index chip so the periphery link lands somewhere real. 4) (Stretch) past ZOOM_LABEL_THRESHOLD, render matched periphery marks on the dashed ring during an active find.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/relationship/PlexPage.tsx:1742-1776 (searchSpace/bestMatch), :632-651 (periphery label); plex-layout.ts; roster/relationship/api/router.py list endpoint (~:1218 state/filters); EntitiesIndexPage.tsx FilterChips.

moves.title: Ego-exclude the Concentration aggregation and wake its staleness axis
moves.why: North star: failure/emptiness never impersonates health and staleness never wears current authority; the page's own spec ('see which entities dominate each relationship type') is defeated when the default answer is the owner at 50.9% and every row is age-blank. Payoff: the headline KPI becomes a real social-concentration signal the owner can act on.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: exclude the owner subject row from items/rollup in get_entities_concentration (keep an explicit 'you → N people' line in the response for the header). 2) Populate last_seen from last_observed_at for interaction_sync edges (or backfill at read time from the fact timestamps). 3) Frontend: render an explicit dim 'age unknown' token when last_seen is null; cap the targets line with a '+N more' overflow instead of 29 inline links.
moves.integration_points: roster/relationship/api/router.py:2254-2400 (concentration query + rollup); ConcentrationPage.tsx:168-322 (row + targets), :261-276 (staleness branch), :346-370 (KPI strip); contract test alongside the bu-hmdqz.5 OpenAPI gate.

moves.title: Close the archive lifecycle: unarchive endpoint, Archived chip, undo-toast
moves.why: th-projects mandate 'every lifecycle closed' + design-bar recovery criterion (undo over confirm for reversible actions — archive is reversible in the data model but irreversible in the product). Payoff: curation becomes fearless; a mis-click no longer silently deletes someone from every list forever.
moves.slice_plan: 1) POST /relationship/entities/{id}/unarchive (mirror of :5180, clears metadata.archived/archived_at). 2) state=archived filter value on the list endpoint + 'Archived' STATE_CHIP on the Index (rows show archived-at and an Unarchive action). 3) Single-archive becomes optimistic with a toast Undo (calls unarchive); keep the bulk serif-gloss confirm. 4) Detail archive stops navigating away blind — toast with Undo instead.
moves.integration_points: roster/relationship/api/router.py:5111-5230 + _VALID_ENTITY_STATES (~:1156); frontend client.ts:3097; EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:118-122, 220-249; EntityDetailPage.tsx:2587-2596.

moves.title: Keyboard parity across the tab family + cursor visibility
moves.why: North star keyboard-first; one visual (and interaction) language built by one hand — three sibling tabs teach j/k/Enter/find and two teach nothing, and the Index cursor can leave the viewport. Payoff: the whole entities family becomes drivable without the mouse, matching the muscle memory the surface already trained.
moves.slice_plan: 1) scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on Index cursor change. 2) Port the Index cursor pattern to Concentration rows (j/k/Enter-opens, number keys switch predicate tabs) and Circles rows (j/k, Enter toggles expand). 3) '/' focuses the local search input on Index/Circles.
moves.integration_points: EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1305-1363, 679-693; ConcentrationPage.tsx (row list ~:452); CirclesPage.tsx:360-396; keep all maps container-scoped per the established never-window-global convention.

moves.title: One ENTITY_TYPES vocabulary for create, filter, and detail
moves.why: Design-bar consistency bias 5 (one vocabulary everywhere); the detail Select silently cannot represent product/group entities the create dialog mints. Payoff: zero-surprise round-tripping and one fewer latent render bug.

audits.page: health — /health overview + /health/{measurements,medications,conditions,symptoms,meals,research} (frontend/src/pages/HealthOverviewPage.tsx, MeasurementsPage.tsx, MedicationsPage.tsx, ConditionsPage.tsx, SymptomsPage.tsx, MealsPage.tsx, ResearchPage.tsx; backend roster/health/api/router.py)
audits.jarvis_gap: The surface is real and wired: every tracker uses QueryBoundary/SourceDegradedNote (no errors impersonating calm), the freshness spine's KPI ages landed and go amber past per-vital SLAs, writes flow through the same fact-store path as butler tools, and the overview briefing degrades honestly to a templated fallback. But the surface only speaks for the half of the owner's body-data it was hardcoded to know: 102/206 live readings (resting_hr, hrv, breathing_rate, active_minutes) have no chart tab, no filter option, and no form representation, while 3 of 7 chart tabs (blood_pressure, blood_sugar, temperature) have zero rows ever and sit as perpetual empty states; opening Edit on 142/206 live rows crashes the form on a TYPE_META lookup. The one live pending attention item (an hrv drift insight the backend classifies as needs-review) renders with a LOW-severity glyph because the frontend reads the priority scale backwards, and its link lands on an unfiltered page whose chart shows weight — the signal→evidence spine breaks at both the severity hop and the last-door hop. The freshness chips tell minority truth (77% of rows carry no source attribution, so the only chip is an 11-day-dead home_assistant rendered in calm gray), trend day-buckets are UTC while every sibling query is owner-tz, and bucket means hide a 33.65kg scale glitch inside a "58.1" weight row. Five-second verification fails not because the page lies about what it shows, but because what it shows is a curated subset wearing whole-record authority.

findings.title: Edit dialog crashes for ~69% of live readings (TYPE_META lookup on out-of-vocabulary types)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementForm.tsx:169 `const unit = TYPE_META[type].unit;` — TYPE_META is Record<MeasurementType,...> keyed on the 5-type union (types.ts:2279-2284: weight, blood_pressure, heart_rate, blood_sugar, temperature). MeasurementTracker.tsx:154-161 renders an Edit button on EVERY row and the list endpoint returns all measurement_* predicates (router.py:209 prefix LIKE). Live census (health.facts, validity=active): resting_hr 31 + hrv 28 + breathing_rate 27 + spo2 24 + steps 16 + active_minutes 16 = 142/206 rows whose Edit click renders MeasurementForm with TYPE_META[type] === undefined → TypeError during render. Also the type <select> (MeasurementForm.tsx:182-188) cannot represent these types, so even absent the crash, editing would coerce the reading through a 5-type vocabulary.
findings.detail: The reading log deliberately shows the full vocabulary (prefix LIKE, raw-type fallback label at MeasurementTracker.tsx:61-63) but hands every row to a form that only understands 5 types. Crash path read directly; not clicked in a browser (read-only rule). This is the taxonomy's 'persistent-but-inert control' worst case: a rendered affordance on majority data that detonates on use.

findings.title: Attention severity inversion: frontend reads insight priority backwards, urgent wears the calm glyph
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/HealthOverviewPage.tsx:291-295 `if (priority <= 1) return "high"; if (priority <= 2) return "medium"; return "low";` vs roster/health/api/router.py:1999-2000 `_HIGH_INSIGHT_PRIORITY = 2` with `priority >= threshold` = needs-review (router.py:2240,2259) and `ORDER BY priority DESC` (router.py:2184). Live: the single pending insight (GET /api/switchboard/insights?butler=health&status=pending) has priority=50, category correlation-drift (hrv upward drift); the briefing counts it as attention (live GET /api/health/briefing → headline "1 health insight needs review", state_class "attention") while AttentionList renders it with the low-severity glyph (AttentionList.tsx:94-103).
findings.detail: Same priority integer, two consumers, opposite polarity. Under the ascending scale every real insight (priority ≥ 2) renders 'low'; a priority-0 nothing-burger would render 'high'. Failure vocabulary inversion on the page's only attention surface.

findings.title: Measurement vocabulary hardcoded in 5 divergent lists; half the live record unchartable/unfilterable, 3 chart tabs perpetually empty (carried-forward eligible, re-confirmed with fresh census)
findings.evidence: CHART_TYPES 7 types (MeasurementChart.tsx:34-42), TYPE_FILTERS 5+all (MeasurementTracker.tsx:43-50), MEASUREMENT_TYPES 5 (MeasurementForm.tsx:31-37), MeasurementType union 5 (frontend/src/api/types.ts:2279-2284), KPI_TYPES 4 (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:311). Live census: resting_hr 31, hrv 28, breathing_rate 27, active_minutes 16 (= 102/206 active rows) appear in NO chart tab and NO filter; blood_pressure, blood_sugar, temperature have 0 rows ever (3 of 7 tabs are permanent 'No data'; 2 of 4 overview KPI slots permanently '—'). Backend is already type-agnostic: list uses prefix LIKE (router.py:209), trend accepts any type string (router.py:1839).
findings.detail: Explicitly eligible for re-promotion this run. The live hrv-drift insight makes the cost concrete: the butler flags a trend in a vital the dashboard cannot chart, filter, or even name in a select. sleep_session/sleep_stage_summary (12+12 rows) live outside the measurement_ prefix entirely — a second invisible tier.

findings.title: Signal→evidence door broken: live insight lands on unfiltered page, chart ignores ?type= entirely
findings.evidence: insightHref default case returns "/health/measurements" (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:285-287) — the live category 'correlation-drift' is unmapped, so the hrv signal opens the unfiltered page. Even for mapped categories, the deep link `?type=X` (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:273-277) is consumed only by MeasurementTracker (MeasurementTracker.tsx:209-212); MeasurementsPage.tsx:21 renders <MeasurementChart /> without initialType, and the chart's activeType is local useState defaulting to "weight" (MeasurementChart.tsx:144). Net: click a blood_pressure signal → the page's leading surface (trend + chart) shows weight.
findings.detail: bu-qvnce.13 landed URL-backed filters on the reading log but the chart — the page's declared leading surface — never joined. Insight metadata carries no vital name in a machine-readable field for the href builder (metadata=null on the live row), so the category→door mapping can't recover it either.

findings.title: Freshness spine tells minority truth: 77% of readings unattributed, sole listed source is 11 days dead and wears calm gray
findings.evidence: Live SQL: 158/206 active measurement rows have no metadata source/provider (max valid_at 2026-07-10); GET /api/health/measurements/sources returns only home_assistant, last_sample_at 2026-07-07 (11d before today). The sources query excludes unattributed rows by design (router.py:1798-1806). FreshnessChips render every chip in muted foreground with no SLA tint, no deadman state (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:209-243) — 'home_assistant · synced 11d ago' in the same calm gray as a fresh source, and the 158 newer unattributed readings appear in no chip at all.
findings.detail: NOT a rediscovery of landed move #13 (which built the sources endpoint + KPI ages — those work). The new instances: (a) write paths still emit unattributed rows (docstring at router.py:1786 claims 'source is the canonical key written at ingest going forward', contradicted by rows created 2026-07-11 with none), so the truth surface silently covers a minority of the record; (b) the chip itself has no staleness vocabulary — a dead feeder and a live one are pixel-identical.

findings.title: Trend buckets truncated in UTC while every sibling query on the surface is owner-timezone
findings.evidence: roster/health/api/router.py:1874 `date_trunc('{trunc_unit}', valid_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')`; live GET /measurements/trend returns naive `"bucket_start":"2026-07-04T00:00:00"`. Contrast: list_measurements resolves owner tz for since/until (router.py:216-226, PR #3075), nutrition summary is owner-tz (router.py:1949-1959), MealTracker day-grouping is owner-tz (PR #3070). For a UTC+8 owner, any reading after 8am lands in the correct day but evening/overnight readings before 8am local shift into the prior UTC day's bucket.
findings.detail: Carried-forward eligible ('owner-tz trend buckets'). The repo already fixed this class of bug three times on this same surface (PRs #3065/#3070/#3075) — trend is the last unconverted query. The trend rule-list prints these UTC day labels as authoritative day rows.

findings.title: Trend rows show bucket mean only — a live sensor glitch renders as a 12kg one-day weight drop with no variance signal
findings.evidence: Live GET /measurements/trend?type=weight&window_days=14: bucket 2026-07-04 has value_mean 58.12, value_min 33.65, value_max 70.35, n=3 (a half-on-scale glitch reading). The API returns value_min/value_max but the trend rule-list renders only value_mean (MeasurementChart.tsx:288-290) plus n; the delta arrow then shows a huge spurious ↑ into 07-05.
findings.detail: The data is real, but presenting an intra-bucket 33.65–70.35 spread as the single number '58.1' gives a glitch mean current-fact authority. Min–max range (already in the payload) or outlier quarantine would make it honest.

findings.title: Two disjoint filter systems on one measurements page: chart date-range is local state, log date-range is URL-backed
findings.evidence: MeasurementChart.tsx:146-147 local useState since/until + its own From/To inputs (311-348); MeasurementTracker.tsx:209-212 URL-backed since/until with its own identical-looking From/To inputs (270-293). Two 'From/To' pairs render on the same page, never sync, and only one survives reload/share.
findings.detail: Same-name controls with different scope and persistence semantics on one screen — a re-read/hunt defect and a dialect drift from the URL-as-source rule the tracker itself documents (MeasurementTracker.tsx:205-208).

findings.title: Heading dialect split across the six-page ledger: 3 pages Dispatch editorial, 3 pages generic list shell
findings.evidence: MeasurementsPage.tsx:10-17, MedicationsPage.tsx:17-25, MealsPage.tsx:158-165 use Eyebrow + Display(44px/500) + Voice; ConditionsPage.tsx:5-13, SymptomsPage.tsx:5-13, ResearchPage.tsx:5-13 use Page archetype="list" whose HeadingBlock renders Title h1 (page.tsx:100-119) and whose loading skeleton is Card chrome (page.tsx:205-213).
findings.detail: All six are siblings under the same HealthLedgerIndex; navigating Measurements→Conditions visibly changes the design language. The bu-w7b18.4 reframe converted tracker internals but left the page shells on the generic archetype.

findings.title: Nutrition totals count only macro-bearing meals while labeled 'meals'; live meals carry nutrition:null and nothing closes the loop
findings.evidence: router.py:1944-1947 'Meals without nutrition data are excluded'; live GET /nutrition/summary (30d window) returns meal_count=0 while GET /meals returns meals in that window (e.g. eaten_at 2026-06-24, nutrition:null). MealsPage.tsx:137 renders `{meal_count} meals · {days} days` — the count silently means 'meals with macros'.
findings.detail: The 'No nutrition data for this window' empty line is honest; the footer count vocabulary is not. Deeper JARVIS gap: the butler logs rich meal descriptions ('a whole container of cookie butter') and no path ever estimates macros, so the totals column is structurally starved.

findings.title: No keyboard/palette path for the hot logging loops on any sub-page
findings.evidence: grep useRegisterCommands across frontend/src/components/health/ and the six sub-pages: zero registrations (only HealthOverviewPage.tsx:386-403 registers two reload verbs). 'Log measurement' (MeasurementTracker.tsx:313), 'Log meal', 'Log dose' are mouse-only buttons.
findings.detail: Carried-forward eligible ('palette logging verbs'). The single most repeated owner action on this surface (logging a reading/dose/meal) has no palette verb and no shortcut, against the keyboard-first north star and the fleet-wide palette-verbs sweep (bu-t64p2) that covered other pages.

audits.ideal: The Health surface is the owner's morning body-glance: the briefing states the one fact that matters today with age-honest vitals, and the entire measurement vocabulary is derived from the data itself — every type the connectors or butler ever wrote gets a chart tab, a filter, a KPI candidacy (top-N by recency and owner pin), and a generic form representation with a unit registry, so no reading the system holds is invisible, unfilterable, or un-editable. Every attention item is a door that opens onto the exact pre-filtered trend it cites (severity polarity identical to the backend's), the chart and log share one URL-backed filter state so any view is shareable and any signal deep-links to its evidence in one hop. Feeders wear their liveness: every write path stamps a source, chips go amber then loud when a feeder exceeds its cadence SLA, and an 'unattributed' bucket is itself a named chip rather than silence. Trend buckets are owner-timezone days with min–max variance bands so a scale glitch reads as a glitch, not a 12kg swing. All six ledger pages speak one Dispatch dialect, and logging a reading, dose, or meal is a palette verb from anywhere; the butler closes its own loops — estimating macros on logged meals (flagged as estimates), quarantining outlier readings for one-tap confirm — so the record stays chartable without owner labor.

moves.title: Data-derived measurement vocabulary end-to-end (kills the Edit crash structurally)
moves.why: North star: 'nothing rendered the system cannot prove' cuts both ways — the system must render what it CAN prove, and today 102/206 live readings are invisible to chart/filter/form while the form crashes on 142/206 (MeasurementForm.tsx:169). Vision's earned-calm requires the surface to speak for the whole record; the live hrv insight flags a vital the UI cannot even name. Owner payoff: every reading the connectors deliver becomes visible, chartable, and safely editable.
moves.integration_points: New GET /api/health/measurements/types (distinct predicate suffix + count + latest + value-shape) in roster/health/api/router.py; replace CHART_TYPES (MeasurementChart.tsx:34), TYPE_FILTERS (MeasurementTracker.tsx:43), MEASUREMENT_TYPES + TYPE_META (MeasurementForm.tsx:31), KPI_TYPES selection (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:311); widen MeasurementType to string with a units/labels registry keyed by known types + generic fallback.
moves.slice_plan: 1) types endpoint + OpenAPI contract test; 2) form: generic value editor + registry fallback (fixes crash, ships alone); 3) chart tabs + tracker filter consume the endpoint (zero-row types drop out, live types appear); 4) overview KPI slots pick owner-pinned or top-4-by-recency vitals.

moves.title: Fix severity polarity + make every insight a one-hop door to its pre-filtered evidence
moves.why: Trace-spine doctrine: 'every clause a door on an unbroken trace signal→session→evidence'. Today the sole live signal wears the wrong severity glyph (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:291-295 inverted vs router.py:2000) and its door opens on an unfiltered weight chart. Owner payoff: five-second verification of what the butler flagged.
moves.integration_points: HealthOverviewPage.tsx insightSeverity (align to ascending priority, thresholds from one shared constant with roster/health/api/router.py:2000); insightHref: map correlation-drift/anomaly categories and require insight writers to stamp metadata.vital + metadata.href; MeasurementsPage.tsx pass useSearchParams type into <MeasurementChart initialType>; merge chart since/until into the tracker's URL params (one filter state, MeasurementChart.tsx:146 / MeasurementTracker.tsx:209).
moves.slice_plan: 1) severity polarity fix + regression test pinning backend threshold; 2) chart consumes ?type=/since/until from URL; 3) insight writer stamps vital metadata + href builder uses it.

moves.title: Attribution-complete freshness spine with per-source deadman vocabulary
moves.why: Doctrine: 'staleness never wears current-data authority; failure never impersonates health'. Live: 158/206 rows unattributed (invisible to the sources truth) and the only chip is an 11-day-dead feeder in calm gray (HealthOverviewPage.tsx:209-243, router.py:1798-1806). Owner payoff: the freshness row becomes the actual answer to 'is my body data flowing'.
moves.integration_points: Every measurement write path (wellness_ingest, measurement_log MCP tool, dashboard POST at router.py:315) stamps metadata.source (owner-manual / butler / connector name); one-time backfill migration for the 158 legacy rows inferable from source_entity_id or created path; FreshnessChips gain per-source cadence SLA (amber past cadence, red 'silent Nd' past 2×) mirroring the landed VITAL_SLA_DAYS pattern; add an 'unattributed · N readings' chip whenever the count is nonzero.
moves.slice_plan: 1) write-path stamping + contract test that /sources sample_count sums to total actives; 2) backfill; 3) chip SLA tint + silent-feeder state; 4) unattributed chip.

moves.title: Owner-tz trend buckets + variance-honest trend rows
moves.why: Fourth instance of the same tz bug class already fixed on this surface (PRs #3065/#3070/#3075) — router.py:1874 still truncates in UTC; and the trend list renders a live glitch bucket (33.65–70.35kg) as flat '58.1' (MeasurementChart.tsx:288). Earned calm requires day labels that mean the owner's days and swings that are real.
moves.integration_points: router.py get_measurements_trend: date_trunc AT TIME ZONE owner_tz (reuse _owner_zoneinfo, router.py:121); TrendBucket already carries value_min/value_max — render range (min–max) beside the mean in the rule-list and a shaded band on the chart; flag buckets where range > k·stddev as 'check reading'.
moves.slice_plan: 1) owner-tz truncation + faketime-bounded test; 2) min–max in rule-list; 3) chart band; 4) outlier flag (optional, can defer).

moves.title: One Dispatch dialect + URL-backed filters + palette logging verbs across all six ledger pages
moves.why: Design-language spec (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language) — one visual language built by one hand; keyboard-first north star. Conditions/Symptoms/Research still wear the generic list shell (ConditionsPage.tsx:5) beside three editorial siblings; meal filters are unshareable local state (MealsPage.tsx:152); the hottest owner actions (log reading/dose/meal) have zero keyboard path while overview ships only reload verbs.
moves.integration_points: Reframe ConditionsPage/SymptomsPage/ResearchPage headers to Eyebrow+Display+Voice (pattern in MedicationsPage.tsx:17-25); lift MealsPage filters to useSearchParams (pattern in MeasurementTracker.tsx:209); useRegisterCommands on each sub-page: 'Log measurement', 'Log dose', 'Log meal', 'Log symptom' opening the respective dialog (command-registry already global, cf. bu-t64p2 sweep).
moves.slice_plan: 1) three page headers; 2) meals URL filters; 3) palette verbs per page (one PR each, independent).

moves.title: Nutrition closure loop: butler-estimated macros with estimate provenance
moves.why: Manifesto-driven proactivity: the butler already captures rich meal prose but live meals carry nutrition:null, so the totals column is structurally starved and the count vocabulary undercounts (router.py:1944, MealsPage.tsx:137). A JARVIS closes its own data loops instead of waiting for the owner to type grams of fat.
moves.integration_points: meal_log tool (src/butlers/tools/health) gains an async post-log estimation step on the cheap tier writing nutrition metadata with {estimated:true}; nutrition_summary and MealsPage distinguish measured vs estimated (e.g. '7 meals · 4 estimated'); DailyTotals footer counts all meals and states macro coverage separately.
moves.slice_plan: 1) honest count copy (S, ships alone: 'N meals with macros · M without'); 2) estimation step + estimate badge; 3) summary splits measured/estimated totals.

audits.page: ingestion — /ingestion (timeline ledger), /ingestion/connectors, /ingestion/connectors/:type/:id, /ingestion/filters
audits.jarvis_gap: The bones are genuinely strong — URL-backed filter/drawer/trace state, honest histogram-sourced hour totals, a freshness badge with a distinct Down state (bu-jad4j.5), degraded-source notes for the three known roster sub-source flags, and a careful, spec-annotated component tree. But the surface's honesty is allowlist-based: only the failures someone pre-identified (hourly_events_available, device_liveness_available, owntracks_cadence_available) get named, while every *query-level* failure across the surface defaults to a calm empty — a dead API renders "No connectors registered." with a zero KPI band, a failed incidents fetch renders "No incidents recorded.", a failed rules fetch renders "No rules at this gate. Policy lives in code.", and a failed histogram renders "0 events" headers above visible rows. Remediation vocabulary lies for non-OAuth connectors (any state=error → a "reauth" pill that full-page-navigates to a raw JSON 501). And the product's densest ledger has zero keyboard surface while Approvals/Dashboard/Issues all adopted the shared useListTriage j/k+verbs primitive — against purpose-and-single-pane.md:40's explicit "Keyboard-first navigation" scope. Un-landed 07-12 knowns observed in one line each: the timeline connector attention strip is still the stale fork (TimelineTab.tsx:781-813, /switchboard/connectors + own health derivation, no archived exclusion); the pause/run-now/disconnect/rotate lifecycle endpoints still have zero reachable pixels (ConnectorDetailView onPause/onRunNow props never passed by ConnectorDetailPage); connector archive is still one-way in pixels (unarchive_connector at ingestion_connectors.py:1029 has no frontend caller). audits.ideal: Open /ingestion and within five seconds know three things with proof: is the house hearing everything right now (a freshness badge that can only say Live/Idle/Down truthfully), which channel needs a hand and the exact remediation verb for it (reauth for OAuth credential failures, restart/bridge-check for transport failures, one keystroke to act), and what any signal cost — every ledger row one keypress from its sessions, replay, payload, and trace spine. Every number on the page is provably sourced or explicitly absent: a failed query is always a named degraded source, never an empty state, a zero, or a stale figure wearing current authority. The ledger is keyboard-native (j/k roving, o/Enter drawer, r replay, x select, / search, published to the ? sheet); the roster folds liveness+state+auth into one verdict word whose remediation action is always real; connector lifecycle (pause, run-now, archive, restore, disconnect, rotate) is one door away from the row it affects; and the filters page states exactly what the code will do to the next event, with a dry-run tester to prove it.

findings.title: Credential/model verify failures are structurally excluded from the /issues failure spine (result=NULL)

Live: 608 action='failed' rows all-time, 275 in the last 7 days (Spotify ACCESS_TOKEN failing right now, row 1314888 owner|failed|s:SPOTIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN|result=NULL at 03:02 today), while GET /api/issues shows 6 groups, none credential-related. The 07-12 'hourly verify' move made this worse by volume: its failures write into a lane the failure feed cannot see. The secrets passport shows probe state locally, but /issues claims 'Grouped errors and warnings across all butlers' and misses an entire failure class — failure impersonating calm on the fleet's canonical failure register.

findings.title: Audit 'From' date filter means UTC-midnight, not owner-midnight — the exact bug class sessions fixed on 07-12, unfixed here
findings.detail: AuditLogPage's From input (type=date) forwards 'YYYY-MM-DD' to ?since=, which FastAPI coerces to a naive midnight datetime compared against ts (timestamptz) in the DB session timezone (UTC). For a +08:00 owner, 'From July 17' silently excludes 00:00-08:00 of July 17 owner-time. sessions.py documents this precise failure ('FastAPI's datetime coercion produces midnight in the DB session timezone, i.e. UTC... excluded everything logged after owner-midnight') and fixed it with _resolve_session_time_bound + owner ZoneInfo — the fix was never applied to the audit-log endpoint. Also asymmetric: there is a 'From' but no 'To', so an incident window from last week cannot be bounded and must be paginated through.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py (since: datetime Query, ts >= $1 with no tz resolution); frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:248-254 (Input type=date → raw since param); src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:102-131, :143-164, :448-450 (the sibling's documented fix for this exact mechanism)

findings.title: Offset pagination + 30s poll makes deep audit pages unstable, and page position is not URL-backed
findings.detail: The audit ledger paginates by LIMIT/OFFSET over ts DESC on a table appending ~2 rows/minute live, with a fixed 30s refetchInterval. While the owner reads page N, each poll re-executes the same offset against a grown table: rows slide across page boundaries, so Next/Previous duplicate or skip evidence rows mid-investigation, and the page the reader is on silently mutates under FetchingDim. Page index is plain component state (useState(0)), so reload/back/deep-link discards position — the one filter state bu-qvnce.13 left out of the URL. The fleet already has a settled answer: keyset cursor pagination (received_at DESC, id DESC with opaque next_cursor) is the documented convention for /api/ingestion/events; the audit ledger — the evidence surface where row stability matters most — doesn't use it. (Also: audit polls a raw 30_000 while the issues feed uses the bus-aware interval; poll-policy widening is fenced by bu-k8888, noted in one line only.)
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:~430 (LIMIT ${idx} OFFSET ${idx+1} over ts DESC); frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx:53 (const [page, setPage] = useState(0)), :87 (offset: page * PAGE_SIZE); frontend/src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts:9 (refetchInterval: 30_000); CLAUDE.md 'Cursor Pagination (BREAKING — Phase 2b)' convention; live meta.total=33316 → 1,666 pages

findings.title: Outcome 'Unknown' copy claims it means pre-unification history, but current-day writers produce it in bulk

Live 7d data falsifies this: verified (798), failed (275), models.verify_all (98), approval.approve (24), approval.deny (16), model.update (10), model.priority (6) — all written this week, all result=NULL. Owner-consequence mutations (approvals, model config) render outcome 'Unknown' today, diluting the column exactly where it matters. Root cause is shared with the critical finding (writers skip the result kwarg on audit_router.append, which accepts it — audit.py:172-184); fixing the append contract fixes both.

Clicking 'View' on a specific group (e.g. 'http-502 approvals', 1 occurrence) lands on ALL error rows for that actor — every group interleaved — because GET /api/audit-log has no error-substring/group-key param the link could carry. The inline occurrences drill mostly compensates, but its Load more caps at 500 while a group's total can exceed it ('Showing 500 of N' with no overflow door), at which point the lossy link is the only continuation. audits.ideal: The issues/audit pair is the fleet's accountability spine and behaves like one instrument. /issues is the single honest register of everything that failed: the audit append boundary enforces that any failure-semantic write carries result='error', so no failure class can be born invisible; groups are windowed, keyed collision-free, one keypress from their raw occurrences, each occurrence one door from its session transcript, and every door in both directions carries the full group predicate. /audit-log is the forensic ledger: 'Privileged' is a true allowlist of owner-consequence mutations (approvals, credentials, config, security) with machine cadence relegated to the noise view; time bounds are owner-timezone calendar days with both a From and a To; pagination is keyset so evidence never shifts under the reader and position survives reload; every active predicate — result, kind, key, actor, action, q — is a visible, dismissible chip; outcome is a genuinely three-valued truth where Unknown means only pre-contract history. Both surfaces share the j/k triage loop, palette verbs name their targets, and the empty state can always prove the difference between 'nothing happened' and 'your filters hid everything'.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the chrome is close to the bar — honest degraded/truncated notes, occurrence drill with true totals, acknowledge-until-recurrence, j/k triage, deterministic-4xx error copy — but the data contract beneath it leaks: 275 credential-probe failures in the last 7 days never reach /issues at all because their writer omits result='error' (the lane's only predicate) and they render as outcome 'Unknown' in the ledger, so the fleet's canonical failure register shows 6 warnings while a credential fails hourly; the 'Privileged only' default is 74% routine llm_api_call/session success rows, defeating the five-second scan it exists for; the From filter silently means UTC-midnight (the exact class sessions fixed on 07-12); deep pages shift under a 30s poll on offset pagination with position lost on reload; and doors from a group to the ledger drop the group's identity because the backend has no text filter to carry it. The gap is not more pixels — it is making the append boundary and the filter predicates as honest as the pixels already claim to be.

audits.page: memory — /memory, /memory/facts/:id, /memory/rules/:id, /memory/episodes/:id (MemoryPage house-ledger: MemoryOverture/MemoryBrowser/AttentionRail/HousekeepingBand + detail trio). NOTE: live stack was DOWN for the entire audit window (butlers-dev containers in 'Created' state, 127.0.0.1:42200 connection-refused); all evidence is source-confirmed against worktree HEAD 4ae7c5598 (= origin/main@46f699036 + 2 schema-routing commits). No open PR touches these files (checked gh pr list files).
audits.jarvis_gap: The house-ledger redesign remains the fleet's best-spoken surface: honest three-way loading/error/empty states on every band (MemoryLoadError, bu-mkd5r), URL-state deep links that round-trip, arm-confirm mutations without modals, a zero-red-when-healthy color discipline, and a KPI/pipeline overture that answers "is remembering working" in under five seconds. What separates it from the ideal is a half-landed honesty spine and two dead ends. PR #3346 (b52cf10a3, 2026-07-17, backend-only) gave every memory endpoint a truthful degraded vocabulary — 503-with-named-pools on detail misses, meta.pools_failed on all four list envelopes — and the frontend consumes it in exactly one place (MemoryOverture). The detail trio still flattens the new 503 into a fabricated "not in the ledger"; the registers and search still print confident undercounted totals when a pool is down. Worse, the page's only red signal (dead letters) drills down to nothing: the DB stores dead_letter_reason, last_consolidation_error, attempts, and next retry on every failed episode, but the API model omits all four, so the owner reaches a red "dead_letter" badge with zero evidence and no requeue action — the one lifecycle on this surface that never closes. The fact page's only mutations fail in total silence (no onError anywhere in the chain). And the keyboard story regressed to mouse-only: the search input's "/" glyph advertises a key that now opens the command menu instead, and the hot loop (review fading facts → confirm each) costs three clicks per fact with no row-level or keyboard path.

The hot loop the rail creates (N important facts fading → review) finishes at keyboard speed: j/k across ledger rows, Enter to open, an arm-confirm 'c' to re-ink in place, so tending the house's beliefs costs seconds, not clicks. A per-butler lens answers "what does the finance butler believe" without leaving the page.

audits.page: qa-system — /qa, /qa/patrols/:id, /qa/investigations/:id (QaOverviewPage.tsx, QaPatrolDetailPage.tsx, QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx + components/qa/*). NOTE: live stack was DOWN during this audit (connection refused on 127.0.0.1:42200; no butlers dev containers running — only butlers-dev-log-cleanup-1 up), so every finding is graded source-confirmed at best; no live reproduction was possible.
audits.jarvis_gap: The QA surface is one of the most doctrine-mature pages in the fleet — breaker tri-state that never defaults to calm, evidence-bearing reset confirm, honest force-patrol toast, failed-state plumbing from move 9, claim-anchored diagnosis with hover-linked evidence. But it still tells three quiet lies and misses the last hop of several spines. (1) The patrol pulse strip paints 'suppressed' patrols — patrols that FOUND novel problems but dispatched nothing — with the same clean-green dot as genuinely clean patrols, so the exact moment the staffer sees trouble and doesn't act renders as health. (2) The page's temporality is render-time-only: the overdue-patrol deadman clause, 'next patrol in Xm', pulse-strip ages, and case ages are all computed once per render with no tick; on a quiet system with an empty case rail (byte-identical refetch payloads → no react-query notify → no re-render) a left-open page never fires the overdue clause — the deadman fails precisely in the quiet-staffer-death scenario it was built for, rescued only accidentally by server-computed age_seconds when cases exist. (3) The dossier's signature claim⇄evidence cross-highlighting is mouse-only (no focus, no keyboard path, title-only claim notes), violating keyboard-first on the page's core evidence spine. Beyond honesty: KPI cells and the verdict's aggregate numbers are not doors (a 'failed · 24h: 3' cell doesn't open the three failed cases), the case rail dead-ends at 25 rows with 'narrow filters to see more', a summary error blanks a perfectly healthy dossier with a retry-less 'Couldn't reach the staffer', and the patrol journal footer asserts 'patrol every 10m' from a hardcoded default rather than the wire's patrol_interval_minutes.
audits.ideal: The ideal JARVIS-grade QA surface is a self-verifying watchdog-of-the-watchdog: the opener verdict re-evaluates on a clock (not just on data change), so 'patrol overdue' fires autonomously within a minute of truth on a page left open overnight; every patrol dot on the pulse strip carries the full backend status vocabulary — clean green, dispatched amber, suppressed as a loud 'saw problems, acted on none' state, skipped/running visually distinct — and every aggregate is a door: each KPI cell opens the exact filtered case set that produced its number, the tripped-breaker clause opens the five failing attempts, a dedup mark opens the case it deduplicated against, and the 8-dot strip ends in a door to full patrol history. The dossier's claim-anchored diagnosis is fully keyboard-traversable (claims are focusable, Enter pins the highlight, evidence rows scroll into view), the case rail pages past 25 rows, degraded sources always name themselves with a retry affordance instead of italic dead-ends, and a running patrol's detail page polls itself until it terminates. Five seconds on /qa answers: did patrols run on time, did any see trouble, was every piece of trouble acted on, and if not — one keystroke to the evidence.

findings.title: Suppressed patrols render the same clean-green dot as clean patrols on the pulse strip
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/QaOverviewPage.tsx:471-478 (statusDotClass: only error/failed→destructive, findings_dispatched→amber, everything else falls through to bg-[var(--green)]) vs src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:1823-1830 (_VALID_PATROL_STATUSES includes 'suppressed' and 'skipped_overlap') and src/butlers/modules/qa/__init__.py:1393-1405 ('suppressed' = novel findings exist but none were dispatched). A patrol that found real problems and acted on none — the breaker-open / all-filtered case — is glanceably indistinguishable from a clean patrol; 'running' and 'skipped_overlap' also read green. Failure-taxonomy shape 12 (backend-wide vs frontend-narrow status vocabulary, unhealthy values falling through to benign). Tooltip shows the raw status but the dot is the glanceable signal.

findings.title: Overdue-patrol deadman and all relative ages are render-time-frozen; on an empty case rail the deadman can never fire
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/qa/QaVerdictOpener.tsx:89-101 (buildOverduePatrolClause computes Date.now() at render; no timer anywhere in dispatch-verdict.tsx), frontend/src/components/ui/time.tsx:391-399 (only 'relative-compact' and 'clock-24h-mono' modes tick; mode="relative" is static), QaOverviewPage.tsx:526-530 (pulse strip uses mode="relative"), CaseList.tsx:28-35 (formatAge plain function). With react-query v5 structural sharing + tracked props, byte-identical 30s refetches produce no re-render; the only per-request-changing field is server-computed age_seconds (src/butlers/api/routers/qa.py:2125-2127), so re-evaluation happens only accidentally when the case list is non-empty. On a quiet system (zero cases in window — exactly the silent-staffer-death scenario the clause guards), a left-open page shows 'QA staffer healthy: next patrol in 10m' indefinitely and never raises 'patrol overdue'.
findings.detail: Staleness wearing current-data authority, and a deadman whose firing depends on unrelated data churn. Fix: a 30-60s tick in QaVerdictOpener (or lift the clause into a component that subscribes to a clock), and mode="relative-compact" or ticking Time for strip/rail ages.

audits.page: qc:ux-truth
sessions — /sessions, /sessions/:id (SessionsPage.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx, components/sessions/*, hooks/use-sessions.ts; live-verified against http://127.0.0.1:42200)
audits.jarvis_gap: The honesty plumbing on this surface is now close to best-in-class: verdict opener, KPI strip, pinned strip, and list all consume degraded fan-out meta and gate their all-clears (bu-hmdqz.12 verified landed), the dossier resolves globally with a distinct pool-down state, and running sessions tick live. But the page's flagship keyboard loop is a mirage — pressing j opens a modal drawer whose aria-modal state suspends every subsequent shortcut, and Esc clears the selection, so the advertised j/k/[/]/y loop can never advance past the first row and the y binding is structurally unreachable (tests mock the drawer, so this never surfaced). Below the UI, the root-evidence layer itself is untrustworthy in a subtler way: the spawner's parser/capture merge keys on incompatible fingerprints (signature-bound apply_defaults vs literal LLM args), so most tool calls persist twice and the dossier renders duplicate rows with contradictory outcome dots — "Tool Calls (8)" for ~5 real calls, grey Unknown beside green Success for the same invocation. Add per-keystroke history/query spam on the free-text filters (a defect class this repo already fixed three times elsewhere) and a "last 24h" window frozen at mount time, and the gap to JARVIS-grade is: the surface tells the truth about what it fetched, but not yet about what happened, and cannot yet be driven at the speed of thought.
audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade sessions surface is the fleet's flight recorder driven entirely from the home row: the page opens with a window-true verdict ("N failed in the last 24h, clustered on X; nearest running Ym"), and j/k genuinely rove the list — a non-modal dossier pane follows the selection live (ticking elapsed for running rows, root evidence for failures) without ever stealing the keyboard, [ / ] page, Enter pins to the full-page dossier, y copies the id, everything the '?' sheet advertises actually fires. Free-text filters settle debounced into a single shareable URL entry. Every evidence layer is exact: the tool-call timeline shows one row per real invocation, pairing arguments to result to an outcome the runtime asserted (never inferred from arguments, never duplicated, never grey-Unknown for a call that succeeded), with retry lineage and correction counts rendered or retired. All windows ("last 24h", pinned "recent") are rolling and stay true in a tab left open for a week, and every count that could be partial names the pool it is missing.

findings.title: j/k/[/]/y keyboard loop is self-suspending: first keypress opens the modal drawer, which suspends all page shortcuts; y is structurally unreachable
findings.evidence: Chain: SessionsPage.tsx:314-360 (j/k call selectSession → sets ?selected=) → SessionsPage.tsx:580-583 (SessionDetailDrawer sessionId={selectedSessionId}) → SessionDetailDrawer.tsx:64 (Sheet open={sessionId != null}) → ui/sheet.tsx:3,7,46 (Radix Dialog, modal default → aria-modal="true") → use-register-shortcut.tsx:157-158 (any [role=dialog][aria-modal=true] suspends ALL page shortcuts; none of the sessions bindings set allowWhenSuspended). Worse, Esc closes the drawer via onClose → selectSession(null) (SessionsPage.tsx:582), clearing selection, so the next j restarts at row 0 (SessionsPage.tsx:317-321) — the loop can NEVER advance past the first row. The y binding (SessionsPage.tsx:344-355) only exists while ?selected= is set, i.e. exactly while the modal is open and it is suspended — unreachable by construction. Tests never caught it because SessionsPage.test.tsx:35 mocks SessionDetailDrawer (no real aria-modal in jsdom); SessionTable.tsx:39-40's comment claims the page syncs DOM focus onto data-session-id, but no code queries [data-session-id] (grep: only writers). The '?' help sheet advertises all five shortcuts as working.
findings.detail: The page's entire keyboard hot loop — its headline discoverability/keyboard-first affordance, published to the shortcut help sheet — is dead on arrival in the live app. This is a fabricated affordance: the product promises a capability it cannot deliver. Fix requires making the selection preview non-modal (Radix modal={false} or an inline preview pane) or exempting the roving bindings via allowWhenSuspended with explicit drawer-scoped handling, plus a regression test that renders the REAL Sheet.

findings.title: Session dossier tool-call timeline double-counts calls and renders contradictory outcome verdicts for the same invocation (parser/capture merge fingerprint mismatch)
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/sessions/ca419914-9c5b-4daa-ba62-6fb8fbe04b76 returns 8 tool_calls for ~5 real invocations — collection_list and item_search each appear twice (one capture record {name,module,result,outcome:'success',input_fingerprint}, one parser record {id,name,input} with no outcome); GET /api/sessions/5c4ec6e7-29ce-4ec0-a69d-c8e19febebee shows the same pair for chronicler_gap_interview. FE renders each parser record as a separate timeline row with a grey 'Unknown' dot (ToolCallTimeline.tsx:298-316) next to the green 'Success' row for the same call, and the section header counts both ('Tool Calls (8)', SessionDossier.tsx:249). Mechanism: merge keys on name|input_fingerprint (spawner_tool_calls.py:152-166), but capture-side fingerprints signature-bound args with apply_defaults() (mcp_wrappers.py:102-111) while parser-side fingerprints the LLM's literal input; verified sha256('null')=74234e98… matches the live executed collection_list fingerprint while the parser's {} hashes to 44136fa3…, and item_search parser args hash to b9b6b8…/b34f9e… vs executed 7815cf…/094fe9… — signatures can never match unless the LLM explicitly passed every default.
findings.detail: The dossier is the root-evidence door on the trace spine; it currently over-reports call counts and attaches an 'Unknown' verdict to calls that demonstrably succeeded, and the argument→result pairing is lost for unmerged calls. Fix belongs at the write seam: fingerprint both sides through one normalization (bind parser args through the same signature+apply_defaults path, or merge by runtime call id echoed through capture), not in the renderer.

findings.title: Free-text filter inputs (Trigger, Request ID) push one browser-history entry AND refire three fan-out query families per keystroke — the exact defect class already fixed on NotificationsPage and for j/k selection
findings.evidence: SessionsPage.tsx:205-213 handleFilterChange calls setSearchParams without {replace:true} and with no debounce; wired to per-keystroke onChange at :433 (Trigger) and :450 (Request ID). Each keystroke changes filterParams + params, re-keying useSessions, useSessionAggregate (KPI strip), and the SessionStripeChart aggregate — each a fan-out across all 11 butler pools (live: GET /api/sessions meta confirms per-pool fan-out via sources_degraded). Contrast NotificationsPage.tsx:176 (replace:true, comment citing this exact defect) and commit 4581ce7e5 (bu-2nnhj) which fixed the same 'N Back-clicks to leave the page' shape for j/k; SessionsPage got the fix only for ?selected= (line 275-282), never for its filter inputs.
findings.detail: Typing a 32-char request id = 32 history entries (32 Back-clicks to leave the page) and ~96 pool-fanning requests. Severity = friction × frequency on the page's primary triage path.

findings.title: Pinned failure rows assert 'no error detail' while the per-row detail fetch is still loading or has failed — loading/failure impersonating a truthful absence
findings.evidence: SessionsPinnedStrip.tsx:233-235 renders `error ? truncate(error) : "no error detail"`; use-sessions.ts:137-142 (useSessionErrorExcerpts) collapses loading, fetch-error, and genuinely-null error all to null (`detail?.error ?? null`). A failed session with a real error message shows the claim 'no error detail' for the entire detail-fetch latency, and permanently if its detail fetch errors.
findings.detail: Taxonomy shape 8/11: needs a tri-state — loading placeholder, 'error detail unavailable' on fetch failure, 'no error recorded' only when the resolved detail truly has error=null.

findings.title: Verdict opener and pinned-failures 'last 24h' window is frozen at mount time — in a long-lived single-pane tab the label silently widens toward 48h+
findings.evidence: SessionsPage.tsx:169-172 memoizes verdictSinceIso with [] deps (cutoffIsoForWindow at :53-55 reads Date.now() once per mount); the bus-aware refetches (use-sessions.ts:43-52,68-73) re-poll forever with that same since= param. SessionsVerdictOpener.tsx:80 renders 'failed in the last 24h' and the pinned strip shares the same cutoff (SessionsPage.tsx:197-201).
findings.detail: Stale window wearing current-data authority (over-reports failures rather than fabricating calm, so minor). Fix: recompute the cutoff per refetch quantized to e.g. 5 minutes so the query key stays cache-stable while the claim stays true.

findings.title: ToolCallTimeline infers a call's outcome from its ARGUMENTS: a tool legitimately invoked with status/state/success-shaped args gets a fabricated Failed/Pending verdict
findings.evidence: ToolCallTimeline.tsx:204-225 outcomeCandidateRecords explicitly pushes `args` (and the raw `input` record) into the outcome-inference pool; outcomeFromRecord (:169-202) reads top-level status/state/outcome/success/exit_code keys from any candidate; inferToolCallOutcome (:227-242) lets any 'failed' candidate dominate. A call like task_update(status="failed") or item_create({status:"rejected"}) renders a red Failed dot even though the invocation succeeded. No live mislabel found in sampled sessions (live inputs nest their status fields one level down), but the path is unguarded.
findings.detail: Latent fabricated-verdict hazard on the evidence surface. Fix posture: infer outcome only from result/error/explicit outcome fields; arguments are inputs, never evidence of outcome. (Largely mooted for merged records once finding 2 is fixed, since capture records carry an explicit runtime-asserted outcome.)

audits.page: settings-secrets — /settings, /settings/permissions, /settings/models, /secrets (SettingsConsolePage.tsx, SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx, SettingsModelsPage.tsx, SecretsPage.tsx + secrets/passport/*). NOTE: live verification unavailable this run — dev stack down (butlers-dev-migrations-1 exited 1 on "Migration failed for: chronicler" from the worktree's local migration-schema-routing commits; dashboard-api/frontend containers stuck in Created). All confidence grades are source-confirmed by mechanism read. Un-landed 07-12 knowns observed in one line each: (1) auth_renewal attention item still routes to /secrets?tab=runtimes (settings_console.py:308) which no frontend code consumes — the focus-grammar repoint never landed (no commit greps for it); (2) ConsoleClock interval leak still present (SettingsConsolePage.tsx:205-210 — cleanup returned from a setTimeout callback is dead code); (3) webhook Delete still fires with zero confirmation (SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1011-1022, 1171-1179) despite the 07-12 "webhook delete confirm" known.
audits.jarvis_gap: Three of the four routes are near the bar: the Settings console has honest-null KPIs, bus-driven live attention, and palette verbs; the Models page carries verification-age/breaker consequence pixels; the Secrets passport is a mature, deep-linkable, degraded-aware book with wired mutations. But the surface fails the JARVIS test exactly where governance meets action. The Permissions matrix — the page whose manifesto question is "what can this system do, on whose authority?" — cannot actually change authority: every default cell arrives inherited=true and the frontend disables inherited cells, so the owner can never write the FIRST explicit revoke for spawn/notify/email.send/calendar.write/cross_butler; the runtime enforcement layer (core/permissions.py) is real but unreachable from its own control surface, and the spec's own "inherited cell is flipped → explicit row" scenario is impossible. Around that dead center, failure still impersonates calm in several joints: /api/approvals/metrics zero-fills on pool loss with no degraded flag (console panel shows a confident "0 approvals pending" during an outage), the console's own approvals/models sub-aggregations return confident 0 / 0-of-0 when no DB is wired, the live attention protocol keys adds/removes by non-unique `kind` so one recovered CLI provider erases sibling red alerts for up to 5 minutes, and the permissions page renders "No recent audit entries." / "No webhooks registered." on fetch errors. Drill-down doors also dead-end (attention overflow routes to /audit-log where the hidden items don't exist; auth_renewal routes to a ?tab= param nothing reads). The gap to JARVIS is not more surface — it is making the one governance control real and making every remaining zero provably earned.
audits.ideal: The ideal settings-secrets surface is the owner's five-second authority console: /settings opens with an attention strip whose every item is a stable-identity door (unique id, deep-links to the exact credential/model/approval it names, overflow expands inline), KPI cells that are either a proven number or an explicit "unavailable: <source>" — never a fabricated zero anywhere in the chain from pool to pixel. /settings/permissions is a live enforcement editor: every cell of the runtime-enforced vocabulary is flippable (first flip creates the explicit row), shows who/why/when on hover, streams the resulting audit entry into the reel within a second, and the reel/webhooks render errors as errors with retry. /settings/models stays continuously true while open (bus-invalidated usage, breaker, and verification state) and speaks the same Dispatch dialect as its siblings. /secrets keeps the passport book but with copy that never overstates ("needs reauth", not "expiring"), no inert affordances, and one-time secret reveals that cannot be accidentally dismissed before the owner confirms storage. Everything hot is reachable by palette and keyboard; every claim traces to a probe, a row, or an honest degraded flag.

findings.title: Permissions matrix cannot create a first explicit grant/revoke — primary control dead, runtime enforcement unreachable from UI
findings.evidence: Backend returns a DENSE matrix where every (butler, perm) pair without an explicit row is PermissionCell(granted=PERMISSION_DEFAULT_GRANTED, inherited=True) (src/butlers/api/routers/permissions.py:120-131); frontend disables exactly those cells: `disabled={inherited}` + "opacity-40 cursor-default" (frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:363-367, default `cell?.inherited ?? true` at :353). onCellFlip is only reachable through that disabled button. Enforcement is real (spawn/cross_butler/notify/email.send/calendar.write gates read public.permissions — src/butlers/core/permissions.py:1-36, readers in core/spawner.py, core_tools/_switchboard.py, _notifications.py, modules/email.py, modules/calendar.py), default-allow with explicit-row revoke — so with no pre-existing row the owner cannot revoke anything from the UI. Contradicts the spec's own scenario: openspec/specs/dashboard-permissions/spec.md:60-61 ("WHEN an inherited cell is flipped THEN the resulting row in public.permissions is explicit") and the page's description copy ("Flip cells to grant or revoke", SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1277). Spec self-contradiction at :43 ("dim/non-editable") vs :60 should be resolved toward flippable.
findings.detail: PUT /api/permissions/{butler}/{perm} happily upserts any pair (permissions.py:157-203), so only the frontend disable stands between the owner and the control. Fix is one line of intent (enable click on inherited cells; modal already collects the reason) plus rendering inherited-vs-explicit as dim-vs-foreground without disabling.

findings.title: /api/approvals/metrics fabricates all-zero calm on pool loss; console Approvals panel and its own sub-aggregations render confident zeros
findings.evidence: approvals.py get_metrics: `if not action_pools: return ApiResponse(data=ApprovalMetrics())` (all-zero defaults, ~:1459-1461) and per-pool `except Exception: logger.warning(...)` with no DegradedSources tracker or meta flag (~:1546-1548) — unlike the sibling /approvals and /history endpoints which set meta.sources_degraded (:1677, :1740). Same shape inside the console aggregator: _count_open_approvals returns (0, None) when db is None — no attention item, confident 0 KPI (settings_console.py:223-224) — and swallows per-pool failures (`except Exception: pass`, :239-240); _count_models returns (0, 0, None) when db is None → confident "0/0" Models OK KPI (:257-258). Contrast _get_spend_mtd which correctly returns (None, None, amber item) on the same condition (:181-191).

findings.title: Attention live-delta protocol keyed by non-unique `kind` — one recovery erases sibling red alerts; adds clobber same-kind items
findings.evidence: Producers emit multiple items sharing a kind: one red auth_renewal per unauthenticated CLI provider (settings_console.py:302-310) and up to four amber subsystem_error items (:424-426, all four helpers use kind="subsystem_error"). Delta computation collapses them into a dict keyed by kind (`old_items = {item["kind"]: item ...}`, :517-521), and the FE reducers do the same: applyAttentionAdd filters out ALL items of the incoming kind before upserting (use-settings-console-live.ts:84-92) and applyAttentionRemove drops every item of the kind (:94-96). So when codex re-authenticates while gemini is still broken, the emitted attention_remove(kind=auth_renewal) hides gemini's red alert until the next REST reseed — POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS = 5 minutes (frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:23).
findings.detail: Fix: give attention items a stable identity (`id = kind + ':' + subject`), key deltas and reducers on it, and render keys accordingly (SettingsConsolePage.tsx:148 already keys rows by `${item.kind}-${idx}`).

findings.title: Permissions page errors impersonate calm empty states (audit reel + webhooks) and bypass the API client layer

[]`, and renders "No recent audit entries." for the error case (:436-441) — isError is dropped. WebhooksSection reload() catches into a transient toast and leaves webhooks=[] → the persistent render is the calm "No webhooks registered." italic (:938-947, :1043-1046). Matrix load failure at least renders "Failed to load matrix." (:1287-1291) but with no retry affordance. The whole page also uses 8 raw `fetch("/api/...")` call sites (:119, :131, :143, :150, :155, :162, :177, :202) — the only page under pages/ doing so — bypassing apiFetch's API_BASE_URL (api/client.ts:419-420), so a non-relative VITE_API_URL silently breaks only this page.

audits.page: spend — /spend (SpendPage.tsx + src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py, live at 127.0.0.1:42200)
audits.jarvis_gap: The page's honesty *scaffolding* is near world-class — degraded notes on every fan-out, verdict opener, fleet-halt banner with session doors, palette verbs, three-way empty/error/partial contracts — but the dollars flowing through that scaffolding are unproven, so the surface currently performs earned calm it has not earned. Live today: the MTD headline reads $23.65 while the same response's solid-actuals chart sums to $55.18 (2.3x, visible as a slope kink where the dashed projection continues at $1.31/day off a $3.07/day solid line); the model breakdown renders "gpt-5.6-luna $0.0000" for the fleet's single most-used model (1,988 calls, 53M input + 66M cached tokens MTD — no pricing.toml entry, silent $0 fallback); $570.92 is attributed to gpt-5.5, a model with zero July ledger rows, because pre-~Jul-10 sessions rows carry the *requested* model while the ledger carries the *executed* one; and the ceiling gate that halts the whole fleet prices from the same luna-blind ledger. Meanwhile the page's own stated core promise ("noticing a spike and capping the schedule that caused it is one continuous motion", SpendPage.tsx:27-29) is impossible: the rule editor's "schedule" purpose option matches nothing (real values are schedule:<task>) and the real values are untargetable. The 07-12 known "breakdown window unification (bu-7o89u)" remains visibly un-landed — one "· 30d" header still spans 30d/calendar-month/all-time windows across its four tabs. Against the north star — nothing fabricated, failure never impersonates health — the page fails at its headline number while passing everywhere else.
audits.ideal: The ideal /spend answers "am I on budget?" from exactly one spine: the same ledger the fleet-halt gate reads, with per-day granularity, where every token row carries the executed model and every model carries either a real price or an explicit billing class ("subscription — $0 marginal", "local — free", "UNPRICED — N calls excluded"). The MTD numeral, forecast chart, movers, top sessions, by-schedule, and breakdown are all restatements of that one spine, so they cannot disagree; a divergence deadman (ledger-vs-sessions token drift) is itself a rendered signal, not a log line. Unpriced usage is loud: the KPI footnotes "excludes 2.0k unpriced luna calls", never silently folding them into a smaller, calmer number. Every evidence row is a door that closes the loop into control: a hot schedule row offers "cap this schedule" pre-filling purpose=schedule:<name>; a hot model offers "route away"; the rule editor's vocabulary is populated from the live ledger's actual purpose values so a rule that can never match is unrepresentable. Keyboard-first throughout: Enter saves the ceiling, rules reorder with arrow keys, palette carries "set ceiling / cap schedule X".

findings.title: Unpriced gpt-5.6 family renders $0 with real-price authority; the ceiling gate and MTD headline are blind to the fleet's most-used model
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=model returns "gpt-5.6-luna": 0.0, "gpt-5.6-sol": 0.0, "gpt-5.6-terra": 0.0 rendered as $0.0000 bars (BreakdownBar, SpendPage.tsx:573-594). Live SQL: token_usage_ledger MTD has gpt-5.6-luna = 1,988 rows / 53.3M input + 65.8M cached + 1.46M output tokens; gpt-5.6-sol = 43 rows / 193M cached tokens. pricing.toml has no gpt-5.6-* entries (only gpt-5.3-codex-spark of the codex runtime is priced, line 89); estimate_session_cost returns 0.0 for unknown models with a server-log-only warning saying 'Add it to pricing.toml to fix' (src/butlers/api/pricing.py:316-333). price_mtd_from_ledger (model_routing.py:1357-1397) uses the same $0, so forecast mtd_usd=$23.65 AND check_monthly_ceiling exclude this usage entirely. All three are codex-runtime catalog entries (model_catalog: luna=workhorse+cheap, sol=reasoning+specialty, terra=reasoning) — if subscription-billed, that policy exists only as an omission indistinguishable from misconfiguration, and contradicts codex-spark being API-priced ($2.09 of the $12.33 7d total). In-repo precedent bu-qcuw4/#2394 already established 'render — for unpriced, never $0.00'.
findings.detail: UI cannot distinguish 'unpriced' (luna) from 'deliberately zero' (ollama) from 'genuinely $0' — all render identically. Fix needs an unpriced-propagating envelope (e.g. unpriced_models on summary/breakdown/forecast) plus explicit pricing or billing-class entries for the gpt-5.6 family.

findings.title: Two spend truths on one page: solid-actuals chart sums $55.18 while the MTD KPI reads $23.65, with no divergence detection
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/spend/forecast — sum of projected=false days = $55.18 (Jul 1-18) vs mtd_usd = 23.645121 in the same response; dashed projection continues at $1.31/day (=23.65/18) off a solid line averaging $3.07/day. By design: days come from the per-butler sessions fan-out (_get_butler_daily_stats_from_db, spend.py:1383-1418) while mtd_usd/projection come from the ledger (spend.py:1420-1452); the docstring admits the fan-out is 'possibly divergent' (spend.py:1420-1424) but nothing measures or renders the divergence. Verified the 7d window (Jul 11-18) reconciles exactly ($12.33 both sides), so the drift is concentrated in Jul 1-10 rows — yet the page renders both authorities equal all month.
findings.detail: The ledger has recorded_at, so per-day granularity is one GROUP BY away — the 'MTD query is month-total only' limitation (spend.py:1367-1370) is self-imposed. Deriving days from the ledger would make chart, KPI, and halt gate one source.

findings.title: Per-model dollars can be attributed to a model that never ran: sessions rows carry the requested model, the ledger the executed one
findings.evidence: Live SQL, travel schema Jul 1-10: travel.sessions shows gpt-5.4-mini = 531,109 input tokens (5 rows) and gpt-5.5 = 5 rows with NULL token sums; public.token_usage_ledger for the same butler/window shows those exact 531,109 tokens as gpt-5.6-luna (4 rows) and zero gpt-5.5 rows anywhere in July. Consequence live on the page: GET /api/spend/breakdown?by=model returns "gpt-5.5": 570.922109 (30d) priced at gpt-5.5 API rates for usage the ledger attributes to other models; travel's $556.51 butler-breakdown figure carries the same authority. Every sessions-fan-out surface (summary by_model, breakdown butler/model, daily, movers, top-sessions) prices from sessions.model (core/sessions.py:642-672 aggregates the sessions table's by-model stats).
findings.detail: The 7d-window exact reconciliation suggests current writes stamp the executed model — the misattribution is concentrated in pre-~Jul-10 rows — but those rows render today with full current-data authority in every 30d view. synthesis.headline: Run 05's QC verdict is the strongest of the five runs — 40 of 48 graded slices of the 07-12 program landed as-designed, 7 with gaps, 1 regressed, 0 failed — and yet the fleet spent the week talking to itself: the single most consequential discovery is the consolidation ouroboros, where the core-spawner spec's mandate to store every session's output as an episode makes memory consolidation consume its own exhaust — ~586 no-op LLM sessions/day and ~31M input tokens in two days on travel alone, drowning 90% of the timeline chronicle, flooding the dashboard Now list, and squeezing the global 3-slot spawn cap (live-confirmed independently by four agents). The one regression is the program's flagship: within 4 days of the 07-12 redeploy the tmp-worktree hotreload ceremony returned, `butlers deploy` has produced zero deployments since its own, and the frozen worktree's two unmerged commits broke the chronicler migration and left the whole dev stack dead for hours during this very run — visible only because the move's own behind-main red clause worked. The second-biggest discovery is that the proactive morning voice is structurally destroyed: quiet-hours suppression deletes rather than parks (212 notifications/14d including every morning report), and the freshly-landed as-designed sleeping producer immediately blacked out the insight channel's only daily slot (0 delivered since 07-13; 1,072 expired lifetime vs 25 delivered). The run names a new arc pathology — landed mechanisms lose to the next producer — and the ranked program leads with breaking the ouroboros, deploy provenance truth, park-don't-delete suppression, and a prompt-dump firewall keyed on structured triggers instead of allowlists.
synthesis.qc_verdict: Across the four QC graders, all 15 moves of bu-hmdqz decompose into 48 graded slices: 40 landed-as-designed (83%, up from 34/46 = 74% on 07-12), 7 landed-with-gaps, 1 regressed, 0 failed — the fleet's execution fidelity is now genuinely high, and most landings were live-proven, not just source-read. Standout landings: move 15.3's sleeping producer closed the loop end-to-end live (producer → context bus → notify suppression gate → honest 'context_bus:sleeping' ledger reason), and move 2.3's dispatch breaker actually opened during a real 07-15 provider burst, paged the owner via the attention ledger, and recovered through its half-open path. The worst landing is move 1 slice 1, graded regressed: the exact pathology the flagship deploy move was named for — serving a frozen tmp .worktrees/ checkout — returned within 4 days; every post-07-12 deployments-ledger row is a boot record impersonating a deployment, the deploy CLI has zero adoption since its own redeploy, and during this run the serving worktree's 2 unmerged commits broke the chronicler migration and killed the dev stack for hours (mitigated only by slice 3's behind-main clause, which honestly showed commits_behind_main=4). The with-gaps cluster shares one shape and it is the run's meta-finding, the next step in the arc (run 03: backend-only honesty flags; run 04: mechanism-real, last-mile-missing): landed mechanisms now decay on contact with the next producer — the timeline unwrap's allowlist was drowned within 4 days by the new schedule:consolidation prompt shape (44/50 head rows machine text, worse than pre-fix), the sleeping producer as-designed suppressed the insight channel's only delivery slot, the conflict radar's dedup left a same-family packed-day fabrication (all_day flag never set at write), the decision lint permanently flags closed beads, and the measurement source key covered only the wellness arms. Fixes keyed on surface patterns, allowlists, and ceremony discipline rot; the program's next fixes must key on structured invariants (trigger_source, lifecycle state, calendar/source identity) and automated gates.

themes.title: Landed mechanisms lose to the next producer (the run-05 arc pathology)
themes.description: The new stage in the run-over-run arc (run 03: backend-only honesty flags; run 04: mechanism-real-last-mile-missing): mechanisms now land as-designed and are then eroded within days by new producers, shapes, or workflows their allowlist/ceremony never covered. Pattern-matched unwraps, hand-listed statuses, and discipline-only protocols decay on contact with the fleet's own velocity. The durable fix shape is structural keys (trigger_source, lifecycle state, source identity) and automated gates, never enumerated surface patterns or coordinator discipline.
themes.exemplars: qc:ux-truth/timeline: move-14 summary unwrap drowned within 4 days of landing by the new schedule:consolidation prompt shape — 44-46/50 live head rows raw machine text, worse than pre-fix; qc:deploy-ci: `butlers deploy` bypassed by the compose-hotreload-from-worktree ceremony it retired, within 4 days, and the frozen worktree's unmerged commits killed the dev stack for hours; qc:routing/eco:proactivity: the as-designed sleeping producer immediately suppressed the insight channel's only daily slot (dark since 07-13); qc:data-truth: decision lint permanently flags two closed beads every Monday.

themes.title: The fleet is talking to itself: the consolidation ouroboros
themes.description: The core-spawner spec mandates storing every memory-enabled session's output as an episode with no maintenance carve-out, so consolidation sessions' own outputs re-enter the consolidation queue forever — a self-sustaining loop spawning ~586 no-op LLM sessions/day on travel alone (~34M uncached tokens/week), multiplied ~4x by residual cross-schema episode misrouting. The grind burns workhorse-tier quota, occupies ~3.5 slot-hours/day of the global 3-slot spawn semaphore that owner-interactive dispatches share, floods every session-listing surface, and its spend is invisible because the models involved are unpriced.
themes.exemplars: eco:inference (critical, live): travel 586/588 sessions in 24h are schedule:consolidation; pending=1 self-refeed observed between beats; qc:ux-truth (live): 1,678 sessions / 31,014,676 input tokens in ~2 days, one ~18.5k-token session per single episode; timeline (live): 179/200 head events are this loop; eco:inference (live): foreign butlers' episodes still landing in travel.episodes post-#3393/#3404.

ranked_moves.title: Break the consolidation ouroboros: maintenance sessions never become episodes
ranked_moves.what: Spec delta to core-spawner (§'store the session output as an episode' gains a maintenance trigger-source exclusion) + spawner carve-out so schedule:consolidation-class sessions never write their own output as episodes; clean up the ~1,800 self-generated episodes; root-cause the residual cross-schema episode misrouting (post-#3393/#3404) that multiplies the loop ~4x; batch N pending episodes per spawned session (vs ~1 today at ~18.5k boilerplate tokens each) with a per-run session cap and a 'backlog not draining' deadman; route this tool-less text-in/JSON-out job to the cheap tier/api lane.
ranked_moves.why: vision.md earned calm / 'nothing fabricated' — consolidation exists to distill the OWNER's life, not butler self-narration; th-engineering readable hot paths + the owner's cost-independence doctrine (no-claude/opencode). This is live production breakage: money, spawn capacity, and every session surface at once.
ranked_moves.evidence: live-confirmed by four independent agents: eco:inference (critical: 586/588 travel sessions in 24h are schedule:consolidation; pending=1 self-refeed observed; spawner.py:2016-2022 stores episodes unconditionally per spec:234), qc:ux-truth (1,678 sessions / 31.0M input tokens in ~2 days), timeline (179/200 head rows), dashboard (Now list flooded). Misrouting live: 48 foreign-butler rows/24h in travel.episodes.
ranked_moves.slices: 1) spec delta + trigger-source exclusion + test asserting no episode after a schedule:consolidation spawn; 2) cleanup migration/script for self-generated episodes; 3) misrouting residual diagnosis + fix; 4) episode batching + per-run cap + backlog deadman; 5) cheap-tier/api-lane transport for tool-less maintenance.
